term_table.lsj_entry_text: τραχ-ύς, εῖα, ύ : Ep. and Ion. τρηχύς, fem. -εῖα, -εῖαν, -είης, neut. -ύ ( Hom. (v. infr.), Hes. Op. 291 , Theoc. 25.74 ); in Ion. Prose fem. τρηχέα, acc. τρηχέαν, gen. τρηχέης, dat. τρηχέῃ (imperfectly preserved in codd.; in Hdt. 4.23 , 9.122 , codd. ABCP have τρηχέη, -έην, -έης, RSV have -εῖα, -εῖαν, -είης; for codd. Hp. v. Kühleweinip. lxxxvi); τρηχείην (before conson.) Simon. 89 codd., A.R. 2.375 codd.; τρηχείης (as pr. n.) Hippon. 47 ; gen. pl. neut. ἐρίων . . τρηχείων GDI 5633.14 (Teos); dual in Trag. τραχεῖ, Ion Trag. 67 :—jagged, λίθος Il. 5.308 ; χαλινοί, opp. λεῖοι, X. Eq. 9.9 , cf. 10.6 ; τ. καὶ γωνιοειδής Thphr. Sens. 65 ; prickly, ἄκανθαι, ἄκανθα, Plu. 2.32e , 138d (both Sup. ); rugged, ἀκτή, ἀταρπός, Od. 5.425 , 14.1 ; as epith. of Ithaca, 9.27 , 10.417 ; so γῆ λιθώδης καὶ τρηχέα Hdt. 4.23 ; Χερσονήσου τῆς Τρηχέης καλεομένης, of the Crimea, ib. 99 ; and freq. in Trag. and Att. of rocky districts, A. Pr. 726 , E. Fr. 1083 ; τὰ τραχέα, τὰ τραχύτατα, X. Cyn. 4.10 , Plu. Flam. 4 ; τ. καὶ χαλεπὴ ὁδός Pl. R. 328e ; also, rough, γλῶσσα Hp. Morb. 2.63 ; ἔρια GDI l. c., PCair.Zen. 287.2 (iii B. C.); σφόγγοι ib. 12.56 (iii B. C.); χῆμαι ib. 82.12 (iii B. C.); σινδόνες (towels, opp. μαλακαί) Gal. 6.418 ; χερσὶ μὴ πάνυ μαλακαῖς, ὥσπερ αὖ μηδὲ τραχείαις, ἀνατρίβειν τὸ σῶμα ib. 417 ; τὰ τ. κατὰ τὰς ἀνωμαλίας ἀλλήλοις ἐμπλεκόμενα ἑνοῦται, τὰ δὲ λεῖα κτλ. Diocl.Fr. 26 ; βλέφαρα Sor. 2.16 , PTeb. 273 intr. (ii/iii A. D.); shaggy, τὰ κάτωθεν τ. καὶ τραγοειδής, of Pan, Pl. Cra. 408d , cf. 420e ; λάσιον καὶ τ. [τὸ κέαρ] . . ἔχοντες Id. Tht. 194e ; τ. σώματα, opp. λεῖα, X. Mem. 3.10.1 ; of the voice, harsh, Pl. Ti. 67c , etc.; esp. of the voice of boys, when it breaks, μεταβάλλειν ἐπὶ τὸ -ύτερον Arist. HA 581a18 ; τὸ τ. τῆς φωνῆς Plu. Mar. 14 ; and of a person, τῇ φωνῇ τ. X. An. 2.6.9 ; also τραχυτάτη γλῶσσα (cf. τραχύστομος) Str. 14.2.28 ; of sounds and their combinations, harsh, opp. λεῖος, σύνθεσις, διάλεκτος, Phld. Po.Herc. 994.32 , 36 :—on τραχεῖα ἀρτηρία, v. ἀρτηρία. of battle and conflict, ὑσμίνη Hes. Sc. 119 ; νιφὰς πολέμοιο Pi. I. 4(3).17(35) , cf. Simon. 89 ; φάλαγγες Tyrt. 12.22 . of natural forces, ῥόθιον A. Pr. 1048 (anap.); -ύτερα τὰ νοσήματα ἀπεργάζεσθαι Pl. Ti. 84c ; of a river, Plu. Alex. 60 , etc.; ἄελλαι A.R. 1.1078 . of persons, their acts, feelings, or conditions, rough, harsh, savage, τ. ἔφεδρος Pi. N. 4.96 ; οὐ τ. εἰμι καταθέμεν I am not niggardly in paying, ib. 7.76 ; Ἡσυχία Id. P. 8.10 ; ἅπας δὲ τ. ὅστις ἂν νέον κρατῇ A. Pr. 35 , cf. 188 (anap.), 326 ; δικαστὴς τ. εἶ Id. Ag. 1421 ; τ. γε . . δῆμος Id. Th. 1049 ; τ. καὶ τεθηγμένους λόγους Id. Pr. 313 ; τ. ὀργή E. Med. 447 ; λεῖον καὶ τ. πάθημα Pl. Ti. 63e ; νόμοι τραχύτατοι Id. Lg. 864c ; τὸ τ. τοῦ ἤθους, τοῦ νόμου, Id. Cra. 406a , R. 452c ; -ύτερα πράγματα Isoc. 7.18 ; εὐνομίη τραχέα λειαίνει smooths the rough places, Sol. 4.35 . Adv. τραχέως, Ion. τρηχέως, rare in the literal sense, roughly, τ. ὑλακτεῖν Plu. Arat. 8 ; neut. as Adv., τρηχὺ φωνῇ ἠπείλει Theoc. 25.74 ; θάλασσα τραχὺ βοᾷ AP 5.179 ( Mel. ). of men's acts, τρηχέως περιέπειν τινά handle roughly, Hdt. 1.73 , 114 ; τραχέως ἔχειν to be rough, harshly disposed, Isoc. 3.33 ; τινι D. 19.45 ; -ύτερον ἄρχειν Isoc. 3.55 ; τ. ἀποκρίνεσθαι Plu. Phoc. 21 , etc.; τ. φέρειν take hardly, Id. Lys. 15 ; rarely τραχυτέρως, Pl. Clit. 406a ; περιέφθησαν τρηχύτατα Hdt. 6.15 . (Prob. cogn. with θράσσω, cf. ἐνθράσσω.)
term_table.greek_sentence: εἴπερ οὖν ἕκαστον τῶν ὀργάνων εἰς ἅπερ ὑγιαῖνον ὠφελεῖ τὴν ἐνέργειαν, εἰς ταῦτα καὶ νοσῆσαν βλάπτει, τῶν μὲν τραχειῶν ἀρτηριῶν ἡ βλάβη στενοχωρία τίς ἐστι, τῶν δὲ μυῶν πλημμελὴς καὶ ἄτακτος κίνησις· τῶν μὲν γὰρ ὡς χωρίων τοῦ πνεύματος, τῶν δ’ ὡς ὀργάνων κινήσεως ἡ βλάβη.
term_table.english_sentence_A: If, then, each of the organs, when diseased, harms the activity in those very respects in which, when healthy, it benefits it, the damage of the rough arteries is a certain narrowness, while that of the muscles is a faulty and disorderly motion; for the damage of the former is as of spaces for the pneuma, that of the latter as of organs of motion.
term_table.english_sentence_B: If, then, each of the organs, when diseased, harms the function in precisely those respects in which, when healthy, it benefits it, the damage of the rough arteries is a kind of narrowness, while that of the muscles is a faulty and disorderly motion; for the damage is to the former as places of the pneuma, to the latter as organs of motion.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ἀρτηρία, Ion. -ιη, ἡ, wind-pipe, ἡ ἀ. μόλις ἀναπνεούσῃ ὑπεσύριζε Hp. Epid. 7.25 , cf. 39 , Pl. Ti. 70d , Arist. HA 493a8 , de An. 420b29 ; ἡτραχεῖα ἀ. (cf. 11 ) Timoth. ap. term_table.greek_sentence: εἴπερ οὖν ἕκαστον τῶν ὀργάνων εἰς ἅπερ ὑγιαῖνον ὠφελεῖ τὴν ἐνέργειαν, εἰς ταῦτα καὶ νοσῆσαν βλάπτει, τῶν μὲν τραχειῶν ἀρτηριῶν ἡ βλάβη στενοχωρία τίς ἐστι, τῶν δὲ μυῶν πλημμελὴς καὶ ἄτακτος κίνησις· τῶν μὲν γὰρ ὡς χωρίων τοῦ πνεύματος, τῶν δ’ ὡς ὀργάνων κινήσεως ἡ βλάβη.
term_table.english_sentence_A: If, then, each of the organs, when diseased, harms the activity in those very respects in which, when healthy, it benefits it, the damage of the rough arteries is a certain narrowness, while that of the muscles is a faulty and disorderly motion; for the damage of the former is as of spaces for the pneuma, that of the latter as of organs of motion.
term_table.english_sentence_B: If, then, each of the organs, when diseased, harms the function in precisely those respects in which, when healthy, it benefits it, the damage of the rough arteries is a kind of narrowness, while that of the muscles is a faulty and disorderly motion; for the damage is to the former as places of the pneuma, to the latter as organs of motion.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: τραχ-ύς, εῖα, ύ : Ep. and Ion. τρηχύς, fem. -εῖα, -εῖαν, -είης, neut. -ύ ( Hom. (v. infr.), Hes. Op. 291 , Theoc. 25.74 ); in Ion. Prose fem. τρηχέα, acc. τρηχέαν, gen. τρηχέης, dat. τρηχέῃ (imperfectly preserved in codd.; in Hdt. 4.23 , 9.122 , codd. ABCP have τρηχέη, -έην, -έης, RSV have -εῖα, -εῖαν, -είης; for codd. Hp. v. Kühleweinip. lxxxvi); τρηχείην (before conson.) Simon. 89 codd., A.R. 2.375 codd.; τρηχείης (as pr. n.) Hippon. 47 ; gen. pl. neut. ἐρίων . . τρηχείων GDI 5633.14 (Teos); dual in Trag. τραχεῖ, Ion Trag. 67 :—jagged, λίθος Il. 5.308 ; χαλινοί, opp. λεῖοι, X. Eq. 9.9 , cf. 10.6 ; τ. καὶ γωνιοειδής Thphr. Sens. 65 ; prickly, ἄκανθαι, ἄκανθα, Plu. 2.32e , 138d (both Sup. ); rugged, ἀκτή, ἀταρπός, Od. 5.425 , 14.1 ; as epith. of Ithaca, 9.27 , 10.417 ; so γῆ λιθώδης καὶ τρηχέα Hdt. 4.23 ; Χερσονήσου τῆς Τρηχέης καλεομένης, of the Crimea, ib. 99 ; and freq. in Trag. and Att. of rocky districts, A. Pr. 726 , E. Fr. 1083 ; τὰ τραχέα, τὰ τραχύτατα, X. Cyn. 4.10 , Plu. Flam. 4 ; τ. καὶ χαλεπὴ ὁδός Pl. R. 328e ; also, rough, γλῶσσα Hp. Morb. 2.63 ; ἔρια GDI l. c., PCair.Zen. 287.2 (iii B. C.); σφόγγοι ib. 12.56 (iii B. C.); χῆμαι ib. 82.12 (iii B. C.); σινδόνες (towels, opp. μαλακαί) Gal. 6.418 ; χερσὶ μὴ πάνυ μαλακαῖς, ὥσπερ αὖ μηδὲ τραχείαις, ἀνατρίβειν τὸ σῶμα ib. 417 ; τὰ τ. κατὰ τὰς ἀνωμαλίας ἀλλήλοις ἐμπλεκόμενα ἑνοῦται, τὰ δὲ λεῖα κτλ. Diocl.Fr. 26 ; βλέφαρα Sor. 2.16 , PTeb. 273 intr. (ii/iii A. D.); shaggy, τὰ κάτωθεν τ. καὶ τραγοειδής, of Pan, Pl. Cra. 408d , cf. 420e ; λάσιον καὶ τ. [τὸ κέαρ] . . ἔχοντες Id. Tht. 194e ; τ. σώματα, opp. λεῖα, X. Mem. 3.10.1 ; of the voice, harsh, Pl. Ti. 67c , etc.; esp. of the voice of boys, when it breaks, μεταβάλλειν ἐπὶ τὸ -ύτερον Arist. HA 581a18 ; τὸ τ. τῆς φωνῆς Plu. Mar. 14 ; and of a person, τῇ φωνῇ τ. X. An. 2.6.9 ; also τραχυτάτη γλῶσσα (cf. τραχύστομος) Str. 14.2.28 ; of sounds and their combinations, harsh, opp. λεῖος, σύνθεσις, διάλεκτος, Phld. Po.Herc. 994.32 , 36 :—on τραχεῖα ἀρτηρία, v. ἀρτηρία. of battle and conflict, ὑσμίνη Hes. Sc. 119 ; νιφὰς πολέμοιο Pi. I. 4(3).17(35) , cf. Simon. 89 ; φάλαγγες Tyrt. 12.22 . of natural forces, ῥόθιον A. Pr. 1048 (anap.); -ύτερα τὰ νοσήματα ἀπεργάζεσθαι Pl. Ti. 84c ; of a river, Plu. Alex. 60 , etc.; ἄελλαι A.R. 1.1078 . of persons, their acts, feelings, or conditions, rough, harsh, savage, τ. ἔφεδρος Pi. N. 4.96 ; οὐ τ. εἰμι καταθέμεν I am not niggardly in paying, ib. 7.76 ; Ἡσυχία Id. P. 8.10 ; ἅπας δὲ τ. ὅστις ἂν νέον κρατῇ A. Pr. 35 , cf. 188 (anap.), 326 ; δικαστὴς τ. εἶ Id. Ag. 1421 ; τ. γε . . δῆμος Id. Th. 1049 ; τ. καὶ τεθηγμένους λόγους Id. Pr. 313 ; τ. ὀργή E. Med. 447 ; λεῖον καὶ τ. πάθημα Pl. Ti. 63e ; νόμοι τραχύτατοι Id. Lg. 864c ; τὸ τ. τοῦ ἤθους, τοῦ νόμου, Id. Cra. 406a , R. 452c ; -ύτερα πράγματα Isoc. 7.18 ; εὐνομίη τραχέα λειαίνει smooths the rough places, Sol. 4.35 . Adv. τραχέως, Ion. τρηχέως, rare in the literal sense, roughly, τ. ὑλακτεῖν Plu. Arat. 8 ; neut. as Adv., τρηχὺ φωνῇ ἠπείλει Theoc. 25.74 ; θάλασσα τραχὺ βοᾷ AP 5.179 ( Mel. ). of men's acts, τρηχέως περιέπειν τινά handle roughly, Hdt. 1.73 , 114 ; τραχέως ἔχειν to be rough, harshly disposed, Isoc. 3.33 ; τινι D. 19.45 ; -ύτερον ἄρχειν Isoc. 3.55 ; τ. ἀποκρίνεσθαι Plu. Phoc. 21 , etc.; τ. φέρειν take hardly, Id. Lys. 15 ; rarely τραχυτέρως, Pl. Clit. 406a ; περιέφθησαν τρηχύτατα Hdt. 6.15 . (Prob. cogn. with θράσσω, cf. ἐνθράσσω.)
term_table.greek_sentence: τῆς μὲν οὖν ἐν ταῖς τραχείαις στενοχωρίας τοὺς παρὰ φύσιν ὄγκους ᾐτιασάμην, τῶν δ’ ἐν τοῖς μυσὶ ﻿ [803] πλημμελῶν κινήσεων τὰς προφάσεις νῦν ἐροῦμεν.
term_table.english_sentence_A: Of the narrowing in the rough [arteries], then, I have assigned the swellings contrary to nature as cause; of the faulty movements in the muscles [803] we shall now state the occasions.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Now, for the constriction in the rough (arteries) I blamed the swellings contrary to nature; of the faulty movements in the muscles [803] we shall now state the causes.

C.); μ. ἀρουραῖος literally the field-mouse, but prob. hamster, Cricetus vulgaris, Hdt. l. c.; prov., μ. πίττης γεύεται, of one who tempted by some apparent good finds himself in inextricable difficulties, 'burn one's fingers', 'catch a Tartar', D. 50.26 ; μῦς . . γεύμεθα πίσσας Theoc. 14.51 ; ὅκως χώρης οἱ μῦς ὁμοίως τὸν σίδηρον τρώγουσιν, i. e. for lack of food, Herod. l. c., cf. Pr. 885a37 , Theoc. 22.48 , etc. gag (as if from μύω), Herod. 3.85 . μυὸς ὦτα, v. μυοσωτίς . (Cf. term_table.lsj_entry_text: πρόφασ-ις, εως, ἡ, (προφαίνω) motive or cause alleged, whether truly or falsely: then, actual motive or cause, whether alleged or not: alleged motive, plea, without implication of truth or falsity, ἐπὶ σμικρῇ π. Thgn. 323 ; νόστου π. γλυκεροῦ κώλυεν μεῖναι Pi. P. 4.32 ; κατὰ θεωρίης πρόφασιν ἐκπλώσας Hdt. 1.29 ; π. ἔχων, ὡς . . Id. 6.133 ; καὶ ἐπὶ μεγάλῃ καὶ ἐπὶ βραχείᾳ π. whether the plea put forward be a trifle or a weighty matter, Th. 1.141 ; τῆς αἰτίας τὴν π. the plea in the case, the basis of the charge, Lys. 9.7 ; τοιαύτας ἔχοντες π. καὶ αἰτίας pleas and motives, Th. 3.13 ; π. ἐπιεικής ib. 9 ; ἀναγκαῖαι Is. 4.20 , D. 54.17 ; προφάσεις ἀληθεῖς λέγοντος pleading what was in fact true, And. 4.17 . falsely alleged motive (or cause), pretext, pretence, excuse, π. ἰδίης ἀβουλίης an excuse for . ., Democr. 119 ; οὔτε τιν' ἔχων π. οὔτε λόγον εὐτράπελον Ar. V. 468 (lyr.); καλλίστην εἶναι π., τιμωρεῖσθαι μὲν δοκεῖν, ἔργῳ δὲ χρηματίζεσθαι Lys. 12.6 : abs. in acc., πρόφασιν in pretence, ostensibly, στενάχοντο γυναῖκες Πάτροκλον π., σφῶν δ' αὐτῶν κήδε' ἑκάστη Il. 19.302 , cf. Hdt. 5.33 , E. IA 362 (troch.), Ar. Eq. 466 , etc.; opp. τὸ ἀληθές, Th. 6.33 : in dat., προφάσει Id. 3.86 ; προφάσει τῶν δημοσίων on the pretence that public debts are owing, OGI 669.15 (Egypt, i A.D.); προφάσιος [εἵνεκεν], προφάσεως ἕνεκα, Hdt. 4.135 , Antipho 6.14 ; προφάσεως χάριν Arist. Pol. 1297a14 ; ἐκ μικρᾶς π. Plb. 2.17.3 ; ἐπὶ προφάσιος Hdt. 7.150 : folld. by an inf., αὕτη γὰρ ἦν σοι π. ἐκβαλεῖν ἐμέ for casting me out, S. Ph. 1034 ; οὔτε . . ἔστιν οὐδεμία π. τοῦ μὴ δρᾶν Pl. Ti. 20c ; π. τοῖς δειλοῖς ἔχει μὴ ἰέναι gives them an excuse or plea for not going, Id. R. 469c ; οὐδεμία σοι π. ἐστιν ὡς . . X. Cyr. 2.2.15 ; εὑρὼν π. term_table.greek_sentence: τῆς μὲν οὖν ἐν ταῖς τραχείαις στενοχωρίας τοὺς παρὰ φύσιν ὄγκους ᾐτιασάμην, τῶν δ’ ἐν τοῖς μυσὶ ﻿ [803] πλημμελῶν κινήσεων τὰς προφάσεις νῦν ἐροῦμεν.
term_table.english_sentence_A: Of the narrowing in the rough [arteries], then, I have assigned the swellings contrary to nature as cause; of the faulty movements in the muscles [803] we shall now state the occasions.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Now, for the constriction in the rough (arteries) I blamed the swellings contrary to nature; of the faulty movements in the muscles [803] we shall now state the causes.

Ph. 25 , etc., dat. ἀμφοῖν Aj. 1264 , etc.:—both, of individuals, Il. 1.363 ; of armies or nations, 2.124 :— Hom. uses only nom. and acc.: from Hom. downwards freq. with pl. Noun or Verb, Il. 2.767 , 7.255 , etc.; ἐξ ἀμφοῖν, = ἐξ ἀλλήλοιν , S. OC 1425 : sts. indecl., h.Cer. 15 , Arist. Top. 118a28 , Theoc. 17.26 , A.R. 1.165 . (For the root cf. ἀμφί.)
term_table.greek_sentence: εἴπερ δ’ ἄμφω ταῦθ’ ὑπάρχοι τοῖς παθήμασιν, ὥστε καὶ πλημμελέσι κινήσεσιν εἶναι καὶ μυῶν, αὐτὰ δὲ ταῦτ’ εἴη τὰ ζητούμενα, ἤδη πέρας ἂν ἡμῖν ἔχοι καὶ ὅδε ὁ λόγος· ἔσται γάρ ποτ’ ἀνώμαλος ἡ ἀναπνοὴ καὶ διά τι τούτων.
term_table.english_sentence_A: And if both these things belong to the affections, so that they are both faulty movements and movements of muscles, and these very things are what is being sought, then this argument too would already have its end for us; for respiration will at some time be uneven also through one of these.
term_table.english_sentence_B: If both of these belong to these affections, so that they are both faulty movements and movements of muscles, and if these are the very things being sought, then this discussion too would already have reached its end; for breathing will sometimes be irregular through one of these as well.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: βάδ-ισις [α], εως, ἡ, walking, going, Ar. Pl. 334 ; βαδίσει χρῆσθαι Hp. Aër. 15 ; of hares, τεχνάζειν τῇ β. X. Cyn. 8.3 ; opp. πτῆσις, ἅλσις, Arist. EN 1174a31 .
term_table.greek_sentence: ὡς γὰρ καὶ ἡ βάδισις ἀνώμαλος γίνεται τῶν ἐν τοῖς σκέλεσι μυῶν ἤτοι τρεμόντων ἢ παλλομένων ἢ σπωμένων, οὕτω καὶ ἀναπνοὴ γίνοιτ’ ἄν ποτε ἀνώμαλος διὰ τοὺς κινοῦντας τὸν θώρακα μῦς, ὡς εἴρηται, βεβλαμμένους.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For just as walking too becomes uneven when the muscles in the legs are either trembling or palpitating or in spasm, so too respiration would at some time become uneven because the muscles that move the thorax have been damaged, as has been said.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For just as walking becomes irregular when the muscles in the legs either tremble or palpitate or are in spasm, so breathing too might sometimes become irregular because the muscles that move the thorax are, as has been said, impaired.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ἀνωμαλ-ία, ἡ, unevenness, irregularity, Pl. R. 547a , Arist. HA 495b2 ; of shape, Str. 16.1.21 ; ἀ. τῶν στοιχείων, as cause of disease, Diocl.Fr. 30 : pl., Epicur. Ep. 2p.53U. Astron., irregular motion, anomaly, ἀ. τῆς κινήσεως Gem. 1.20 , cf. Ptol. Alm. 3.3 , etc.; ἀ. ἐκλειπτικαί, of the moon's orbit, Plu. term_table.greek_sentence: ὥστε καὶ πασῶν τῶν ἀνωμαλιῶν, τῶν τε κατὰ μίαν ἐνέργειαν καὶ τῶν κατὰ πολλὰς ἑξῆς συνισταμένων, ἤτοι στενοχωρία τῶν τραχειῶν ἀρτηριῶν, ἢ τῶν τοῦ θώρακος μυῶν πλημμελὴς κίνησις, ἢ ἀῤῥωστία τῆς δημιουργούσης αὐτὴν δυνάμεως αἴτιον γενήσεται.
term_table.english_sentence_A: So that of all the unevennesses, both those which arise within a single activity and those which arise over many in succession, the cause will be either narrowing of the rough arteries, or faulty movement of the muscles of the thorax, or weakness of the faculty that produces it.
term_table.english_sentence_B: So for all the irregularities, both those within a single activity and those that arise across many successive activities, the cause will be either constriction of the rough arteries, or faulty movement of the muscles of the thorax, or weakness of the faculty that produces it.

term_table.english_sentence_A: Now the matters pertaining to the use are, as was also said before, common, and those pertaining to the rough arteries are analogous to those of the smooth ones; but what belongs to the respirations as peculiar and exceptional in comparison with the pulses is the class of the muscles.

term_table.greek_sentence: τὰ μὲν οὖν τῆς χρείας, ὡς καὶ πρόσθεν εἴρηται, κοινὰ, καὶ τὰ τῶν ἀρτηριῶν δὲ τῶν τραχειῶν ταῖς λείαις ἀνάλογον· ἴδιον δὲ ἐξαίρετον ταῖς ἀναπνοαῖς παρὰ τοὺς σφυγμοὺς τὸ τῶν μυῶν ὑπάρχει γένος.
term_table.english_sentence_A: Now the matters pertaining to the use are, as was also said before, common, and those pertaining to the rough arteries are analogous to those of the smooth ones; but what belongs to the respirations as peculiar and exceptional in comparison with the pulses is the class of the muscles.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Now the factors pertaining to the need (χρεία), as was also said before, are common, and those of the rough arteries are analogous to those of the smooth; but what belongs peculiarly and exclusively to respirations, as distinct from pulses, is the class of the muscles.

term_table.greek_sentence: ᾗ μὲν γὰρ αἰτίαι δραστικαί εἰσι, ταύτῃ μὲν ἀνάλογον ἔχουσιν, ᾗ δὲ τῆς ἀναπνευστικῆς δυνάμεως ἡ προαίρεσις ἐπιτροπεύει, τῆς ζωτικῆς δὲ οὐδεὶς ἀνώτερος κύριος, ἀλλ’ ἐλευθέρα τελείως ἐστὶν, ταύτῃ διαφέρουσιν.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For insofar as they are active causes, in this respect they stand in analogy; but insofar as choice (προαίρεσις) governs the respiratory faculty, whereas of the vital faculty there is no higher master, but it is completely free, in this respect they differ.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Insofar as they are efficient causes, in this respect they are analogous; but insofar as choice (προαίρεσις) governs the respiratory faculty, whereas the vital faculty has no higher master but is perfectly free, in this respect they differ.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: περισσός, Att. περιττός, ή, όν, (from περί, as ἔπισσαι from ἐπί, μέτασσαι from μετά) beyond the regular number or size, prodigious, δῶρα Hes. Th. 399 (never in Hom. ); ῶʼμος Trag.Adesp. 458.3 ; στάθμα, dub.sens., v. ἕλκω B. 3 . out of the common, extraordinary, strange, ἔ τι περισσὸν εἰδείη if he has any signal knowledge, Thgn. 769 ; εἴ τι φρονεῖς καί τι περισσὸν ἔχεις Philisc.( PLG 2.327 ); π. λόγος S. OT 841 ; ἄγρα E. Ba. 1197 (lyr.); πάθος Id. Supp. 791 (lyr.); βίος οὐδὲν ἔχων π. ἀλλὰ πάντα σμικρά Antipho Soph. 51 ; οὐ γὰρ π. οὐδὲν οὐδ' ἔξω λόγου πέπονθας E. Hipp. 437 ; περισσότερα παθήματα Antipho 3.4.5 ; τὰ π. τῶν ἔργων καὶ τερατώδη Isoc. 12.77 ; ἴδια καὶ π. Id. 15.145 ; π. καὶ θαυμαστά Arist. EN 1141b6 ; πρᾶξις π. Id. Pol. 1312a27 ; οὐθὲν δὴ λέγοντες π. φαίνονταί τι λέγειν Id. Metaph. 1053b3 ; τί π. ποιεῖτε; Ev.Matt. 5.47 ; περιττοτάτη φύσις Arist. HA 531a9 ; συνανθρωπίζον . . πάντων περισσότατον, of the dog, Ath. 13.611c , cf. Clearch. 24 ; in Literature, striking, τὸ περιττόν, as a quality of οἱ τοῦ Σωκράτους λόγοι, Arist. Pol. 1265a11 ; τὰ σοφὰ καὶ τὰ π. refinements, Epicur. Fr. 409 ; opp. κοινὸς καὶ δημώδης, Longin. 40.2 (but also, elaborate, π. καὶ πεποιημένος Id. 3.4 ; in bad sense, far-fetched, D.H. Pomp. 2 , Dem. 56 ). of persons, extraordinary, remarkable, esp. for great learning, π. ὢν ἀνήρ E. Hipp. 948 ; τοὺς . . π. καί τι πράσσοντας πλέον Id. Fr. 788 ; δυστυχεῖς εἶναι τοὺς π. Arist. Metaph. 983a2 ; π. γένος τῶν μελιττῶν Id. GA 760a4 : freq. with the manner added, π. κατὰ φιλοσοφίαν Id. Pr. 953a10 ; περὶ τὸν ἄλλον βίον περιττότερος somewhat extravagant or eccentric, Id. Pol. 1267 b24 ; τῇ φύσει π. Id. HA 622b6 ; κάλλει Plu. Demetr. 2 ; ἐν ἅπασι Id. Dem. 3 ; τὴν ὥραν Alciphr. 1.12 : c. inf., D.H. Comp. 18 . c. gen., περισσὸς ἄλλων πρός τι beyond others in . . , S. El. 155 ; θύσει τοῦδε περισσότερα greater things than this, AP 6.321 (Leon. Alex. ); περιττότερος προφήτου one greater than . . , Ev.Matt. 11.9 . more than sufficient, superfluous, αἱ π. δαπάναι X. Mem. 3.6.6 ; περιττὸν ἔχειν to have a surplus, Id. An. 7.6.31 ; οἱ μὲν . . περιττὰ ἔχουσιν, οἱ δὲ οὐδὲ τὰ ἀναγκαῖα . . Id. Oec. 20.1 : c. gen., τῶν ἀρκούντων περιττά more than sufficient, Id. Cyr. 8.2.21 ; τὰ π. τῶν ἱκανῶν Id. Hier. 1.19 : freq. in military sense, οἱ π. ἱππεῖς the reserve horse, Id. Eq.Mag. 8.14 ; οἱ π. τῆς φυλακῆς ib. 7.7 ; π. σκηναί spare tents, Id. Cyr. 4.6.12 (but τοῖς περιττοῖς χρήσεσθαι their superior numbers, Id. An. 4.8.11 , cf. Cyr. 6.3.20 ); τὸ π. the surplus, residue, Inscr. ap. eund. An. 5.3.13 (but τὸ π. τοῦ Ἰουδαίου the advantage of the Jew, Ep.Rom. 3.1 ); Ἁρπυιῶν τὰ π. their leavings, AP 11.239 ( Lucill. ); τὸ π. τῆς ἡμέρας the remainder of the day, X.Eph. 1.3 ; π. γράμματα supplementary provisions in a will, BGU 326ii9 (ii A.D.). in bad sense, superfluous, useless, οὐδέ τι τοῦ παντὸς κενεὸν πέλει οὐδὲ π. Emp. 13 ; μόχθος π. A. Pr. 385 , cf. S. Ant. 780 ; π. κἀνόνητα σώματα Id. Aj. 758 ; βάρος π. γῆς ἀναστρωφώμενοι Id. Fr. 945 ; ἄχθος Id. El. 1241 (lyr.); τὰ γὰρ π. πανταχοῦ λυπήρ' ἔπη Id. Fr. 82 ; αὐδῶ σε μὴ περισσὰ κηρύσσειν A. Th. 1048 ; π. πάντες οὑν μέσῳ λόγοι E. Med. 819 ; π. φωνῶν Id. Supp. 459 . excessive, extravagant, μηχανᾶσθαι περισσά commit extravagances, Hdt. 2.32 ; περισσὰ δρᾶν, πράσσειν, to be over-busy, S. Tr. 617 , Ant. 68 ; π. φρονεῖν to be over-wise, E. Fr. 924 (anap.); ἡ π. αὕτη ἐπιμέλεια τοῦ σώματος Pl. R. 407b ; μῆκος πολὺ λόγων π. Id. Lg. 645c ; redundant, overdone, οἱ καρτεροὶ καὶ π. λόγοι Id. Ax. 365c , etc.; of dress, ἐσθὴς π. Plu. 2.615d ; περισσοτέρα λύπη 2 Ep.Cor. 2.7 ; τοῦ τὰ δέοντ' ἔχειν περιττὰ μισῶ I hate extravagance in comparison with moderation, Alex. 254 , etc. of persons, over-wise, over-curious, περισσὸς καὶ φρονῶν μέγα E. Hipp. 445 , cf. Ba. 429 (lyr.); ὁ πολυπράγμων καὶ π. Plb. 9.1.4 ; τὴν περὶ τὸ σῶμα θεραπείαν ἀκριβὴς καὶ π. Plu. Cic. 8 ; so, of speakers, π. ἐν τοῖς λόγοις Δημοσθένης Aeschin. 1.119 . as a term of praise, subtle, acute, ἀκριβὴς καὶ π. διάνοια Arist. Top. 141b13 . Arith., ἀριθμὸς π. an odd, uneven number, opp. ἄρτιος, Epich. 170.7 , Philol. 5 , Pl. Prt. 356e , etc.; π. ἡμέραι Hp. Aph. 4.61 ; τὸ π. καὶ τὸ ἄρτιον the nature of odd and even, Pl. Grg. 451c , etc.; π. χῶραι the odd places in a verse, Heph. 5.1 ; ἀρτιάκις π. ἀριθμός a number divisible by an odd number an even number of times, as 2 , 6 , 10 , Euc. 7 Def. 9 . περισσότεροι more in number, extra, Carnead. ap. S.E. M. 9.140 . περιττόν, τό, = στρύχνος μανικός, θρύον 11 , Thphr. HP 9.11.6 ; περισσόν Dsc. 4.73 ; περίσκον Orib. 12.8.56 . Adv. περισσῶς extraordinarily, exceedingly, θεοσεβέεες π. ἐόντες Hdt. 2.37 ; ἐπαινέσεται π. E. Ba. 1197 (lyr.); π. παῖδας ἐκδιδάσκεσθαι to have them educated overmuch, Id. Med. 295 ; περιττοτέρως τῶν ἄλλων far above all others, Isoc. 3.44 ; περισσότερον τοῦ ἑνός Luc. Pr.Im. 14 ; also περισσά Pi. N. 7.43 , E. Hec. 579 , etc. remarkably, περισσότερον τῶν ἄλλων θάψαι τινά more sumptuously, Hdt. 2.129 ; οἴκησις π. ἐσκευασμένη Plb. 1.29.7 ; περιττότατα ἔχειν to be most remarkable, Arist. HA 589a31 ; κοσμουμένη π. καὶ σεμνῶς Plu. 2.145e ; περισσότατα ἀνθρώπων θρησκεύειν in the most singular way, D.C. 37.17 ; ἡδέως καὶ π. in an uncommon manner, D.H. Comp. 3 ; εἰπεῖν στρογγύλως καὶ π. Id. Is. 20 ; ἰδίως καὶ π. Plu. Thes. 19 ; τὰ καινῶς ἱστορούμενα καὶ π. Id. 2.30d . abundantly, ἐχέτω π. τῆς κρόκης Alciphr. 3.41 . with a neg., οὐδὲν περισσὸν τούτων nothing more than or beyond these, Antipho 3.4.6 ; οὐδὲν τῶν ἄλλων περιττότερον πραγματεύεσθαι Pl. Ap. 20c ; οὐδὲν π. ἢ εἰ . . no otherwise than if . . , Id. Smp. 219c ; περισσόν alone, furthermore, LXX Ec. 12.12 ,al. τὰ περισσά in vain, AP 12.182 ( Strat. ). ἐκ περιττοῦ superfluously, uselessly, Pl. Prt. 338c , Sph. 265e ; but ὑπερέχειν ἐκ π. to be far superior, Id. Lg. 734d , cf. 802d ; ἡ κάμινος ἐκαύθη ἐκ π. Thd. Da. 3.22 ; ἐκ π. χρησάμενος τῇ παρρησίᾳ Luc. term_table.greek_sentence: ἔστι δὲ διττὸν, τὸ μὲν ἀπ’ αὐτῆς τῆς ψυχικῆς δυνάμεως μόνης ὁρμώμενον, τὸ δ’ ἀπὸ τῆς πρὸς τὰς ὀδύνας συμπλοκῆς· ὀλίγον μὲν καὶ δυσγνώριστον τὸ ἀπὸ τῆς [805] δυνάμεως μόνον, πλεῖον δὲ καὶ σαφέστερον καὶ ποικιλώτερον τὸ διὰ τὰς ὀδύνας.
term_table.english_sentence_A: And it is twofold: the one proceeding from the psychic faculty itself alone, the other from its entanglement with pains; that from the [805] faculty alone is slight and hard to recognise, while that due to the pains is greater, clearer and more varied.
term_table.english_sentence_B: It is twofold: the one proceeding from the psychic faculty itself alone, the other from its combination with pains. That which comes from the [805] faculty alone is slight and hard to recognise; that which comes about through pains is greater, clearer and more varied.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: παραφροσύνη, ἡ, wandering of mind, derangement, Pl. Sph. 228d , Aps. p.333 H. delirium, Hp. Aph. 2.2 , 6.53 (pl.), Prog. 10 .
term_table.greek_sentence: ἐν γὰρ ταῖς παραφροσύναις ἐπικρατεῖ μὲν ἡ ἀραιότης καὶ τὸ μέγεθος, ἐμφαίνεται δέ τις ἀνωμαλία καὶ ἀταξία κατά τε πλείους ἀναπνοὰς καὶ κατὰ μίαν ἐνίοτε μόνην, ὡς ἂν, οἶμαι, καὶ τῶν φαντασμάτων ποτὲ μὲν μᾶλλον, ποτὲ δ’ ἧττον ἐξιστάντων τοῦ κατὰ φύσιν τὸν λογισμόν.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For in deliriums rarity and largeness predominate, but a certain irregularity and disorder also appears, both over several respirations and sometimes in a single one alone, inasmuch as, I suppose, the phantasms too at one time more, at another less, displace the reasoning from its natural state.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For in deliria infrequency and largeness predominate, but a certain irregularity and disorder shows itself both over several breaths and sometimes within a single one alone. This is, I think, because the phantasms at one time more, at another less, displace the reasoning from its natural state.

term_table.greek_sentence: ἐν γὰρ ταῖς τοιαύταις φαντασίαις εὔλογον καὶ τὴν ἀναπνοὴν μεταβάλλεσθαί τι καὶ ποικίλλεσθαι πρὸς τὴν τῆς ἀνωμαλίας τε καὶ ἀταξίας γένεσιν καὶ παρὰ τὸ τῆς χρείας ποσόν.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For in such imaginings it is reasonable that the respiration too should change somewhat and become varied, towards the generation of irregularity and disorder, and contrary to the quantity of the need.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For in such impressions it is reasonable that respiration too should undergo some change and variation, towards the generation of irregularity and disorder, and contrary to the quantity of the need.

term_table.greek_sentence: ἕως μὲν γὰρ ὀλίγον αὐτῆς ἑκάστη τῶν ἐνεργειῶν ἀπολείπεται, μικρὰ τοῦ κατὰ φύσιν ἡ ἐναλλαγή· ἐπειδὰν δὲ τοῦ κατὰ φύσιν ἔλλειμμά τι ἱκανῶς πολὺ γένηται, τότ’ ἀναγκαῖον ἤδη τῶν μὲν ἡσυχιῶν τὸ ποσὸν, τῶν δὲ κινήσεων οὐ τὸ ποσὸν μόνον, ἀλλ’ ἤδη καὶ τὸ ποιὸν ἀλλοιοῦσθαι, κᾀν τούτῳ τὴν ὅλην ἀναπνοὴν ἀνώμαλόν τε καὶ ἄτακτον γενέσθαι.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For so long as each of the activities falls short of it by only a little, the alteration from the natural state is small; but when a sufficiently large deficiency relative to the natural state arises, then it is now necessary that the quantity of the rests, and of the movements not only the quantity but now also the quality, be altered, and thereby that the whole respiration become irregular and disordered.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For so long as each of its activities falls only a little short, the departure from the natural state is small. But when the deficiency relative to the natural state becomes considerable, then it is already necessary that the quantity of the rests be altered, and that in the movements not only the quantity but also the quality be altered, and in this way the whole respiration becomes irregular and disordered.

term_table.english_sentence_A: For not even in their case is the need fulfilled in each activity; for they are able to dilate the thorax neither quickly nor frequently nor to the greatest extent; for all these things are [806] distressing to them, most of all the magnitude, second the speed, and then frequency as well; for it is less painful for those in pain to be moved over a longer time than over a shorter one.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For in those cases, too, the need is not fulfilled in each activity; for they are able to dilate the thorax neither [806] quickly nor frequently nor to the greatest extent. For all these things are painful to them: most of all the size, second the speed, and then also the frequency; for it is less distressing for those in pain to be moved over a longer time than over a shorter.

Arch.Pap. 3.134 (Thera, iii/ii B.C.). devotion, affection, goodwill, τᾷ π. ἃν ἔχων τυγχάνει ἐς τὰν ἁμὰν πόλιν SIG 721.30 (Crete, ii/i B.C.), cf. 593.4 (Perrhaebia, ii B.C.); ἀποδεξάμενον μετ' εὐνοίας τὴν τοῦ δήμου π. the homage of the people, ib. 700.43 (Macedonia, ii B.C.); ἐπαινέσαι ἐπὶ τᾷ περὶ . . τὰν τέχναν π. her devotion to her art, ib. 738.11 (Delph., i B.C.), cf. 737.12 (i B.C.); = σπουδή , zeal, τὴν π. ἣν ὁ δῆμος . . διατελεῖ ποιούμενος τῶν . . ἐνδόξων ib. 590.33 (Cos, ii B.C.). expressed opinion, advice, τὴν π. ἀποδεξάμενοι τοῦ λέγοντος Plb. 39.3.9 , cf. 2.42.4 , 7.13.4 , 7.14.1 .
term_table.greek_sentence: ὅσον οὖν ἀπλήρωτον τῆς χρείας ἀπολείπεται, τοῦτ’ ἐν πολλαῖς ἑξῆς ἐνεργείαις ἀθροιζόμενον, ὅταν ἐγγὺς ἤδη τοῦ πνίγεσθαι τὸ ζῶον ἀφίκηται, τότε καὶ τὴν προαίρεσιν ἀναγκάζει, μέχρι γοῦν χρόνου τινὸς, μείζονά τε ποιήσασθαι τὴν ἀναπνοὴν καὶ θάττονα πολὺ καὶ τῆς ἔμπροσθεν πυκνοτέραν.
term_table.english_sentence_A: Therefore whatever portion of the need is left unfulfilled, accumulating over many successive activities, when the animal has already come near to being suffocated, then compels the choice too, for some time at least, to make the respiration greater and much quicker and more frequent than before.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Whatever portion of the need, then, is left unfulfilled, this, accumulating over many successive activities, when the animal has now come close to being choked, then compels the choice as well, at least for some time, to make the breathing larger, much quicker, and more frequent than before.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: μέγας, μεγάλη [α], μέγα, gen. μεγάλου, ης, ου , dat. μεγάλῳ, ῃ, ῳ, acc. μέγαν, μεγάλην, μέγα; dual μεγάλω, α, ω; pl. μεγάλοι, μεγάλαι, μεγάλα, etc.: the stem μεγάλο- is never used in sg. nom. and acc. masc. and neut., and only once in voc. masc., ὦ μεγάλε Ζεῦ A. Th. 822 (anap.). big, of bodily size: freq. of stature, εἶδος. . μ. ἦν ὁράασθαι Od. 18.4 ; κεῖτο μ. μεγαλωστί Il. 16.776 ; ἠΰς τε μ. τε Od. 9 . 508 ; φῶτα μέγαν καὶ καλόν ib. 513 ; καλή τε μεγάλη τε 15.418 ; κάρτα μεγάλη καὶ εὐειδής Hdt. 3.1 ; φύσιν τίν' εἶχε φράζε; Answ. μέγας S. OT 742 . full-grown, of age as shown by stature, νῦν δ' ὅτε δὴ μ. εἰμί Od. 2.314 ; μήτε μέγαν μήτ' οὖν νεαρῶν τινα A. Ag. 358 (anap.); later, elder of two persons of the same name, Wilcken Chr. 305 (iii B. C.); Σκιπίων ὁ μ. Plb. 18.35.9 . of animals, μ. ἵπποι, βοῦς, σῦς, Il. 2.839 , 18.559 , Od. 19.439 ; αἰετός Pi. I. 6(5).50 . generally, vast, high, οὐρανός, ὄρος, πύργος, Il. 1.497 , 16.297 , 6.386 ; wide, πέλαγος, λαῖτμα θαλάσσης, Od. 3.179 , 5.174 ; long, ἠϊών, αἰγιαλός, Il. 12.31 , 2.210 : sts. opp. ὀλίγος, κῦμα οὔτε μέγ' οὔτ' ὀ. Od. 10.94 ; but usu. opp. μικρός or σμικρός, πρὸς ἑαυτὸ ἕκαστον καὶ μ. καὶ σμικρόν Anaxag. 3 ; τὸ ἄπειρον ἐκ μεγάλου καὶ μικροῦ Arist. Metaph. 987b26 , etc. of quality or degree, great, mighty, freq. epith. of gods, ὁ μ. Ζεύς A. Supp. 1052 (lyr.), etc.; μεγάλα θεά, of Demeter and Persephone, S. OC 683 (lyr.); θεοὶ μεγάλοι, of the Cabiri, IG 12(8).71 (Imbros), etc.; Μήτηρ μ., of Cybele, SIG 1014.83 (Erythrae, iii B. C.), 1138.3 (Delos, ii B. C.); Μήτηρ θεῶν μ. OGI 540.6 (Pessinus), etc.; Ἴσιδος μ. μητρὸς θεῶν PStrassb. 81.14 (ii B.C.); μ. ἡ Ἄρτεμις Ἐφεσίων Act.Ap. 19.28 ; τίς θεὸς μ. ὡς ὁ θεὸς ἡμῶν; LXX Ps. 76(77).13 ; ὁ μ. θεός Ep.Tit. 2.13 ; of men, μ. ἠδὲ κραταιός Od. 18.382 ; ὀλίγος καὶ μ. Callin. 1.17 , etc.; μέγας ηὐξήθη rose to greatness, D. 2.5 ; ἤρθη μ. ib. 8 ; βασιλεὺς ὁ μ., i. e. the King of Persia, Hdt. 1.188 , etc. (θεῶν β. ὁ μ., of Zeus, Pi. O. 7.34 ); βασιλεὺς μ. A. Pers. 24 (anap.); as a title of special monarchs, Ἀρδιαῖος ὁ μ. Pl. R. 615c ; ὁ μ. Ἀλέξανδρος Ath. 1.3d ; ὁ μ. ἐπικληθεὶς Ἀντίοχος Plb. 4.2.7 , etc.; μ. φίλος E. Med. 549 ; πλούτῳ τε κἀνδρείᾳ μ. Id. Tr. 674 ; ἐπὶ μέγα ἦλθεν ἰσχύος Th. 2.97 . strong, of the elements, etc., ἄνεμος, λαῖλαψ, Ζέφυρος, Od. 19.200 , 12.408 , 14.458 ; of properties, passions, qualities, feelings, etc., of men, θάρσος, πένθος, ποθή, etc., 9.381 , Il. 1.254 , 11.471 , etc.; ἀρετή Od. 24.193 , Pi. O. 8.5 ; θυμός Il. 9.496 , E. Or. 702 ; κλέος Il. 6.446 ; ἄχος 9.9 ; πυρετός Ev.Luc. 4.38 (incorrect acc. to Gal. 7.275 ); ἡ μ. νοῦσος epilepsy, Hp. Epid. 6.6.5 , cf. Gal. 17(2).341 . of sounds, great, loud, ἀλαλητός, ἰαχή, πάταγος, ὀρυμαγδός, Il. 12.138 , 15.384 , 21.9 , 256 ; θόρυβοι, κωκυτός, S. Aj. 142 (anap.), E. Med. 1176 ; οὐκ ἔστι ὅκως τι νεῖκος ἔσται ἢ μέγα ἢ σμικρόν Hdt. 3.62 ; μὴ φώνει μέγα S. Ph. 574 . generally, great, mighty, ὅρκος Il. 19.113 ; ὄλβος, τιμά, Pi. O. 1.56 , P. 4.148 ; μ. λόγος, μῦθος, a great story, rumour, A. Pr. 732 , S. Aj. 226 (lyr.); ἐρώτημα a big, i. e. difficult, question, Pl. Euthd. 275d , Hp.Ma. 287b ; weighty, important, τόδε μεῖζον Od. 16.291 ; μέγα ποιέεσθαί τι to esteem of great importance, Hdt. 3.42 , cf. 9.111 ; μέγα γενέσθαι εἴς τι X. HG 7.5.6 ; μ. ὑπάρχειν πρός τι Id. Mem. 2.3.4 ; μέγα διαφέρειν εἴς τι Pl. Lg. 78o c; οὐκ ἂν εἴη παρὰ μέγα τὸ δικολογεῖν not of great importance, Phld. Rh. 2.85 S. ; τὸ δὲ μέγιστον and what is most important, Th. 4.70 , cf. 1.142 ; οἱ μέγιστοι καιροί the most pressing emergencies, D. 20.44 ; μ. ὠνησάμενοι χρημάτων for large sums, Plb. 4.50.3 , etc. with a bad sense, over-great, μέγα εἰπεῖν to speak big, and so provoke divine wrath, Od. 22.288 ; λίην μέγα εἶπες 3.227 , 16.243 ; μέγα ἔργον 3.261 , Pi. N. 10.64 ; ἔργων μ. A. Ag. 1546 (anap.); ὠμὸν τὸ βούλευμα καὶ μ. Th. 3.36 ; ἔπος μ., μ. λόγοι, S. Aj. 423 (lyr.), Ant. 1350 (anap.); μ. γλῶσσα ib. 127 (anap.); μηδὲν μέγ' εἴπῃς Id. Aj. 386 ; μὴ μέγα λέγε Pl. Phd. 95b ; μὴ μεγάλα λίαν λέγε Ar. Ra. 835 ; μέγα φρονεῖν S. OT 1078 , E. Hipp. 6 ; μεγάλα φρονεῖν Ar. Ach. 988 ; μεγάλα, μεῖζον ἢ δικαίως πνεῖν, E. Andr. 189 , A. Ag. 376 (lyr.); μέγα τι παθεῖν X. An. 5.8.17 ; μὴ μέγα λέγων μεῖζον πάθῃς E. HF 1244 . of style. impressive, Demetr. Eloc. 278 ; μεῖζον more striking, ib. 103 . of days, long, Gal. 12.714 . Adv. μεγάλως [α] greatly, mightily, Od. 16.432 , Hes. Th. 429 , Hdt. 1.16 , 30 , al., X. Cyr. 8.2.10 , Parth. 28.1 , etc.; strengthd., μάλα μ. Il. 17.723 ; δμαθέντες μ. A. Pers. 907 (lyr.); with Adjs., Hdt. 1.4 , 7.190 . more freq. neut. sg. μέγα as Adv., very much, exceedingly, μ. χαῖρε all hail!, v. l. for μάλα in Od. 24.402 ; esp. with Verbs expressing strong feeling, μ. κεν κεχαροίατο Il. 1.256 ; μ. κήδεται 2.27 , etc.: with Verbs expressing power, might, μ. πάντων . . κρατέει 1.78 ; ὃς μ. πάντων. . ἤνασσε 10.32 ; πατρὸς μ. δυναμένοιο Od. 1.276 , cf. Hom. Epigr. 15.1 , A. Eu. 950 (anap.), E. Hel. 1358 (lyr.), Ar. Ra. 141 , Pl. R. 366a ; μ. δύνασθαι παρά τινι Th. 2.29 ; πλουτέειν μ. Hdt. 1.32 ; or those expressing sound, loudly, μ. ἰάχειν, ἀῧσαι, βοῆσαι, εὔξασθαι, ἀμβῶσαι, Il. 2.333 , 14.147 , 17.334 , Od. 17.239 , Hdt. 1.8 (also pl., μεγάλ' εὔχετο Il. 1.450 ; μ. αὐδήσαντος, μ. ἤπυεν, Od. 4.505 , 9.399 ): strengthd., μάλα μ. Il. 15.321 ; μ. δ' ἔβραχε φήγινος ἄξων 5.838 , etc.: so in Trag. with all kinds of Verbs, μ. στένειν, σθένειν, χλίειν, A. Ag. 711 (lyr.), 938 , Ch. 137 : also in pl., μεγάλα. . δυστυχεῖς Id. Eu. 791 (lyr.). of Space, far, μέγα προθορών Il. 14.363 ; ἄνευθε μέγα far away, 22.88 ; οὐκ ἂν μέγα τι τῆς ἀληθείας παρεξέλθοις Pl. Phlb. 66b . with Adjs., as μέγ' ἔξοχος, μέγα νήπιος, Il. 2.480 , 16.46 ; μ. νήπιε Orac. ap. Hdt. 1.85 ; μ. πλούσιος Id. 1.32 , 7.190 ; ὦ μέγ' εὔδαιμον κόρη A. Pr. 647 : with Comp. and Sup. , by far, μέγ' ἀμείνονες, ἄριστος, φέρτατος, Il. 4.405 , 2.82 , 16.21 . degrees of Comparison (regul. μεγαλώτερος, -ώτατος late, EM 780.1 , 2 ): Comp. μείζων, ον , gen. ονος, Ep. , Att. (also Delph., SIG 246 H 260 (iv B. C.)); Ion. , Arc. , Dor. , Aeol. μέζων, ον , Heraclit. 25 , Hp. Acut. 44 , Hdt. 1.26 , IG 7.235.16 (Oropus), 5(2).3.18 (Tegea), Epich. 62 (also early Att. , IG 12.22.65 , but [με] ίζων ib. 6.93 , by analogy of ὀλείζων ib. 76 , 95 ); dat. pl. μεζόνεσσι Diotog. ap. Stob. 4.7.62 : written μέσδων in Sapph. Supp. 7.6 , Plu. Lyc. 19 : cf. μέττον· μεῖζον, Hsch. (dub.); later μειζότερος 3 Ep.Jo. 4 (used as title, elder, POxy. 943.3 (vi A. D.), etc.); μειζονώτερος A. Fr. 434 :—greater, longer, taller, Il. 3.168 , 9.202 , etc.; freq. also, too great, γέρας Pl. Sph. 231a ; Μηνόφιλος μείζων M. the elder, Ostr.Bodl. v C 2 (ii A. D.); as title, μειζων κώμης headman of a village, POxy. 1626.5 (iv A. D.), etc.: generally, the higher authority, PLond. 2.214.22 (iii A. D.), POxy. 1204.17 (pl., iii A. D.); οὔτε μεῖζον οὔτε ἔλαττον, a strong form of denial, nothing whatever, D.H. Comp. 4 ; οὐδαμὰ προὔφηνεν οὔτε μείζον' οὔτ' ἐλάττονα S. Tr. 324 . Adv. μειζόνως E. Hec. 1121 , Th. 1.130 , X. Cyn. 13.3 , Isoc. 9.21 , etc.; Ion. μεζόνως Hdt. 3.128 , Herod. 4.80 , etc.: neut. as Adv., μεῖζον σθένειν S. Ph. 456 , E. Supp. 216 ; μ. ἰσχύειν D. Ep. 3.28 ; ἐπὶ μ. ἔρχεται S. Ph. 259 . Sup. μέγιστος, η, ον , Il. 2.412 , etc.: neut. as Adv., μέγιστον ἴσχυσε S. Aj. 502 ; δυνάμενος μ., c. gen., Hdt. 7.5 , 9.9 : with another Sup. , μέγιστον ἐχθίστη E. Med. 1323 : in pl., χαῖρ' ὡς μέγιστα S. Ph. 462 ; θάλλει μ. Id. OC 700 (lyr.); τὰ μέγιστ' ἐτιμάθης Id. OT 1203 (lyr.); ἐς μέγιστον ib. 521 ; ἐς τὰ μ. Hdt. 8.111 :—late Sup. μεγιστότατος PLond. 1.130.49 (i/ii A. D.). (Cf. Skt. majmán- 'greatness', Lat. magnus, Goth. mikils 'great'.)

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ἀνα-πνοή, poet. ἀμπν-, ἡ, recovery of breath, μόχθων ἀμπνοά rest from toils, Pi. O. 8.7 , cf. E. IT 92 , etc.; ἀμπνοὰν ἔστασαν they recovered breath, took fresh courage, Pi. P. 4.199 ; ἀ. διδόναι, παρέχειν, E. Andr. 1137 , Pl. Ti. 70d ; λαμβάνειν Id. Phdr. 251e ; ἀναπνοὴν ἔχει . . εἰπεῖν has breath enough to say, Men. 536.6 . respiration, breathing, Pi. P. 3.57 , Ar. Nu. 627 , Pl. Ti. 33c , etc.; including εἰσπνοή and ἐκπνοή, Arist. Resp. 471a7 ; ἀμπνοὰς ἔχειν, = ἀναπνεῖν , breathe, live, S. Aj. 416 ; τὴν ἀ. ἀπολαβεῖν τινος strangle, Plu. Rom. 27 ; ὑπὸ τὴν ἀ. in a breath, Plb. 10.47.9 . = εἰσπνοή , inspiration, opp. ἐκπνοή, Pl. Ti. 78e , 79e , cf. Arist. Resp. 480b10 . exhalation, Thphr. HP 6.2.4 . breathing organ, of the nose and mouth, D.S. 2.12 , Luc. Nigr. 32 . air-hole, vent, Pl. Ti. 85a , 91b , Plu. Aem. 14 .— Only sg. in Pi. ; only pl. in Trag.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ταχύς [υ], εῖα, ύ : of motion, swift, fleet, opp. βραδύς, of persons and animals, either abs., Il. 18.69 , etc.; or more fully, πόδας ταχύς 13.249 , 482 , 17.709 , etc.; ταχὺς ἔσκε θέειν Od. 17.308 ; θείειν τ. Il. 16.186 , Od. 3.112 ; κύνες, ἔλαφος, πτώξ, ἵππος, Il. 3.26 , 8.248 , 17.676 , 23.347 , etc.; οἰωνόν, ταχὺν ἄγγελον 24.292 , cf. Od. 15.526 ; τ. βαδιστής a quick walker, E. Med. 1182 ; σφοδροὶ καὶ τ. X. Cyr. 2.1.31 . of things, τ. πόδες Il. 6.514 , cf. Od. 13.261 , etc.; τ. ἰός, ὀϊστοί, Il. 4.94 , Od. 22.3 , etc.; πτερά Ar. Av. 1453 ; -ύτατα ἅρματα Pi. O. 1.77 ; νῆες, τριήρεις, Hdt. 8.23 , Th. 6.43 , etc.; [ ἴχνοσ] τὸ τοῦ ποδὸς μὲν βραδύ, τὸ τοῦ δὲ νοῦ ταχύ E. Ion 742 . of thought and purpose, quick, hasty, φρονεῖν γὰρ οἱ ταχεῖς οὐκ ἀσφαλεῖς S. OT 617 : c. inf., βλάπτειν τ. Ar. Ra. 1428 ; τ. βουλεῦσαί τι ἀνήκεστον Th. 1.132 , cf. 118 , Luc. Dem.Enc. 12 ; also τ. πρὸς ὀργήν Plu. Cat.Mi. 1 ; τὸ ταχύ speed, haste, E. Ph. 452 , X. Eq. 7.18 , etc. of actions, events, etc., rapid, sudden, πήδημα S. Aj. 833 ; ᾅδης, μόρος, E. Hipp. 1047 , Mosch. 3.26 ; πόλεμος Th. 4.55 , 6.45 ; φυγή Id. 4.44 ; μεταβολή Pl. R. 553d ; short, τ. ἐλπίδες fleeting hopes, Pi. P. 1.83 ; ἐπαυρέσεις Th. 2.53 ; ἀτραπός Ar. Ra. 127 ; ταχεῖ σὺν χρόνῳ S. OC 1602 ; τ. διήγησις short, rapid, Arist. Rh. 1416b30 . Adv., regul. ταχέως, quickly, opp. βραδέως, Il. 23.365 , Hes. Th. 103 , etc.:—rarely in sense perhaps (cf. τάχα 11 ), Plb. 16.25.8 . the Adv. is also expressed by periphr., διὰ ταχέων in haste, Th. 1.80 , 3.13 , Pl. Ap. 32d , X. An. 1.5.9 ; ἐκ ταχείας S. Tr. 395 ; cf. τάχος 11 . neut. ταχύ as Adv., Pi. P. 10.51 , N. 1.51 , S. Ph. 349 , E. HF 885 (lyr.), Ar. Eq. 109 , Gal. 16.665 , etc.; ἤδη ἤδη τ. τ. Sammelb. 4321.21 , BGU 956.3 (both iii A.D.); ἄρτι ἄρτι τ. τ. Arch.Pap. 5.393 (ii A.D.); also τάχα (q.v.). the Adj. ταχύς is freq. construed with Verbs, where we should use the Adv., ταχέες δ' ἱππῆες ἄγερθεν Il. 23.287 ; ταχεῖά γ' ἦλθε χρησμῶν πρᾶξις A. Pers. 739 ; ὁρμάσθω ταχύς S. Ph. 526 ; δεῦρ' ἀφίξεται τ. Id. OC 307 ; τ. χάρις διαρρεῖ Id. Aj. 1266 , cf. Th. 2.75 , 5.66 . Degrees of Comparison: Comp. : the form ταχύτερος, α, ον, is used by Hdt. , ἐποίησα ταχύτερα ἢ σοφώτερα 3.65 , cf. 7.194 ; also in Arist. Mu. 394b3 , Arr. Ind. 9.6 , Aret. SD 1.16 , but not in good Att. ; ταχύτερον as Adv., Hdt. 4.127 , 9.101 , Hp. Prog. 17 . the more usual form is θάσσων, neut. θᾶσσον, gen. ονος, Att. θάττων, neut. θᾶττον, Il. 15.570 , 13.819 (elsewh. only neut. in Hom. ), etc.:—neut. as Adv., freq. in Hom. , Od. 2.307 , al.; θᾶσσον ἂν . . κλύοιμι sooner, i.e. rather, would I hear, S. Ph. 631 ; θᾶσσον also often stands for the Positive, Il. 2.440 , Od. 15.201 , 16.130 , Pi. P. 4.181 , Ar. Nu. 506 , V. 187 , Ra. 94 ; οὐ θᾶσσον οἴσεις; i.e. make haste and bring, S. Tr. 1183 , cf. OT 430 ; θᾶττον νοήματος quicker than thought, X. Mem. 4.3.13 , cf. Ar. V. 824 , etc.; with a Conj., ὅτι θᾶσσον, like ὅτι τάχιστα , Theoc. 24.48 ; ἐπειδὴ θᾶττον συνεσκότασεν as soon as . . , D. 54.5 ; ἐπειδὰν θ. συνιῇ τις Pl. Prt. 325c ; ὅταν θ. φθέγγηται ὁ κόκκυξ Arist. HA 563b17 , cf. 611a5 ; ἐὰν or ἢν θ. as soon as . . , X. Cyr. 3.3.20 , An. 6.5.20 , Pl. Alc. 1.105a ; ἂν θ. Men. Pk. 174 ; εἰ θ. Pl. Ep. 324b ; ὡς θ. Plb. 1.66.1 , 3.82.1 ; θ. rarely = sooner than, before, ἐξήλαυνον μεσημβρίας οὐ πολλῷ τινι θ. Aristid. Or. 51 ( 27 ). 13 (cf. τάχιον infr. 3 ). the form ταχίων [ι], neut. ιον, is freq. in late Prose, as LXX Wi. 13.9 , 1 Ma. 2.40 , Ph. Bel. 69.14 , 17 , 73.23 , Gem. 1.20 , D.H. 6.42 , D.S. 20.6 , J. (v. infr.), Plu. 2.240d , Ev.Jo. 20.4 , Alciphr. 3.4 ; also in Hp. Mul. 1.1 , Men. 402.16 ; but condemned by Phryn. 58 , Hdn. Philet. p.436 P.; τὴν ταχίονα τῆς τροφῆς παράθεσιν earlier, sooner, Gal. 19.206 :—Adv. τάχιον earlier, πλέεται . . περὶ τὸν Σεπτέμβριον μῆνα . . , οὐδὲν δὲ κωλύει κἂν τ. Peripl.M.Rubr. 24 ; τ. τῆς ὑποσχέσεως sooner than they had promised, Rev.Ét.Gr. 6.159 (Iasus); τ. τοῦ παραγγέλματος J. BJ 4.4.2 ; εἰς μακρὸν αὐτῶν γῆρας καὶ βίου μῆκος ὅμοιον τοῖς τ. ἐπερχομένων Id. term_table.greek_sentence: ὅσον οὖν ἀπλήρωτον τῆς χρείας ἀπολείπεται, τοῦτ’ ἐν πολλαῖς ἑξῆς ἐνεργείαις ἀθροιζόμενον, ὅταν ἐγγὺς ἤδη τοῦ πνίγεσθαι τὸ ζῶον ἀφίκηται, τότε καὶ τὴν προαίρεσιν ἀναγκάζει, μέχρι γοῦν χρόνου τινὸς, μείζονά τε ποιήσασθαι τὴν ἀναπνοὴν καὶ θάττονα πολὺ καὶ τῆς ἔμπροσθεν πυκνοτέραν.
term_table.english_sentence_A: Therefore whatever portion of the need is left unfulfilled, accumulating over many successive activities, when the animal has already come near to being suffocated, then compels the choice too, for some time at least, to make the respiration greater and much quicker and more frequent than before.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Whatever portion of the need, then, is left unfulfilled, this, accumulating over many successive activities, when the animal has now come close to being choked, then compels the choice as well, at least for some time, to make the breathing larger, much quicker, and more frequent than before.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: πυκνός, ή, όν, poet. also πυκινός, ή, όν, both forms in Ep. (v. infr.) and Lyr., Pi. O. 13.52 ( Sup. ), B. Fr. 1 ; Aeol. πύκνος Sapph. 1.11 , Alc. HP 1.5.5 ; πλεύμων Plu. 2.698b ; χωρία ib. 650d ; πυκινὴν νάπαις Ἄζιλιν Call. Ap. 89 ; [ὁ ἐλαιὼν] πυκνός ἐστι τοῖς φυτοῖς overgrown with plants, PFay. 113.8 (i/ii A.D.); ξοῒς χαρακτὴ π. Hom. ll. cc.); freq. of thick foliage, ὕλη, λόχμη, θάμνοι, ὄζοι, ῥωπήϊα, δρυμά, πέταλα, Il. 18.320 , Od. 19.439 , 5.471 , Il. 21.245 , Od. 14.473 , 10.150 , 19.520 ; π. νέφεα Hes. term_table.lsj_entry_text: ἄλγ-ημα, τό, pain felt or caused, suffering, S. Ph. 340 , Hp. VM 6 , E. Fr. 507 , Plu. Sull. 26 , Plot. 6.1.19 ; οὐκ ἔστι λύπης ἄ. μεῖζον Men. 667 .
term_table.greek_sentence: ἀλλ’ ἐν ταῖς ταύτης ἐνεργείαις, τῆς μὲν χρείας πληρουμένης, ἀποκναιομένου δὲ τοῖς ἀλγήμασι τοῦ ζώου, πάλιν ἡ προαίρεσις ἀφαιρεῖ καὶ τοῦ μεγέθους καὶ τοῦ τάχους καὶ τῆς πυκνότητος, ἄλλοτε ἄλλου πλέον, ὡς ἂν ἀπορουμένη [807] τε καὶ μήτε στῆσαι τὴν ἐνέργειαν δυναμένη, φόβῳ πνίξεως, μήθ’ εὑρίσκουσά τινα τῆς ὀδύνης ἴασιν.
term_table.english_sentence_A: But in the activities of this [breathing], while the need is being fulfilled, yet the animal is being worn down by the pains, the will again subtracts both from the magnitude and from the speed and from the frequency, at one time more from one, at another from another, inasmuch as it is at a loss [807] and is able neither to halt the activity, for fear of suffocation, nor to find any cure for the pain.
term_table.english_sentence_B: But in the activities of this [breathing], while the need is being fulfilled but the animal is being worn out by the pains, choice once again takes away from the size, the speed and the frequency, at one time more from one, at another time more from another, as though it were at a loss [807] and neither able to stop the activity, for fear of suffocation, nor finding any cure for the pain.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: καταμόνας, Adv. alone, apart, better divisim κατὰ μόνας, v. μόνος B. 111 .
term_table.greek_sentence: κᾀνθένδε τό τ’ ἀνώμαλον ἑκάστῳ τε καταμόνας καὶ ἁπάσαις ἑξῆς ταῖς ἀναπνοαῖς, καὶ τὸ πολυει δῶς ἄτακτον ὑπάρχει.
term_table.english_sentence_A: And from this arises the unevenness, both in each breath singly and in all the breaths in succession, and the manifold disorder.

Spir. 482b15 , Resp. 479b19 , al., Gal. 6.149 , 8.453 - 765 ; τῶν ς. ἅψασθαι Id. 19.207 : metaph. of a vibration of the earth, οἷον ς. Arist. Mete. 366b15 , cf. Plu. Alex. 35 . metaph., οἷον ἐν ς. γενομένης τῆς ψυχῆς Id. Cor. 21 ; unhealthy excitement, Diog.Oen. 57 : pl., Plu. 2.565d .
term_table.greek_sentence: ἐδείχθη γὰρ καὶ τοῦτο ἐν τοῖς περὶ διαφορᾶς σφυγμῶν, ὡς ἡ μὲν ἐφεξῆς ἰσότης ὁμαλότης ἐστὶν, ἡ δὲ κατὰ περιόδους τάξις· καὶ ὡς τῆς μὲν ἐφεξῆς ἰσότητος διαφθειρομένης, ἡ ἀνωμαλία, τῆς δὲ κατὰ περιόδους, ἡ ἀταξία γίγνεται.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For this too was shown in the books On the Differences of Pulses, that equality in succession is evenness, while equality according to periods is order; and that when the equality in succession is destroyed, unevenness arises, and when that according to periods is destroyed, disorder.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For this too was shown in the work on the differences of pulses: that consecutive equality is regularity, while periodic equality is order; and that when consecutive equality is destroyed, irregularity arises, and when periodic equality is destroyed, disorder.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ἀταξία, Ion. -ιη, ἡ, indiscipline, prop. among soldiers, opp. εὐταξία, Hdt. 6.11 , Th. 2.92 , X. HG 3.1.9 , etc. generally, disorder, confusion, ἀ. καὶ ἀκολασία Pl. Cri. 53d ; ἀμαθία καὶ ἀ. X. Ath. 1.5 ; ἀ. καὶ ἀναρχία Arist. Pol. 1302b28 ; εἰς τάξιν ἤγαγεν ἐκ τῆς ἀ. Pl. Ti. 30a ; ἀπὸ τύχης καὶ ἀ. Arist. PA 641b23 : in pl., ἀταξιῶν, opp. τῶν ἐν ταῖς κινήσεσι τάξεων, Pl. Lg. 653e . c. gen., διαίτης ἀ. irregularity, Hp. Coac. 211 ; νόμων Aeschin. 3.38 .
term_table.greek_sentence: ἀλλ’ ὅμως πολλῆς μὲν ἀνωμαλίας, πολλῆς δὲ ἀταξίας ταῖς τοιαύταις διαθέσεσι ﻿ [808] συμπιπτούσης, ἐπικρατεῖ τὸ κατὰ μικρότητα καὶ πυκνότητα γένος τῆς δυσπνοίας.
term_table.english_sentence_A: But nevertheless, although much irregularity and much disorder befall such conditions, [808] the kind of dyspnoea characterised by smallness and frequency prevails.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Nevertheless, although much unevenness and much disorder occur in such conditions [808], the class of difficulty of breathing that consists in smallness and frequency prevails.

term_table.greek_sentence: εἰ γὰρ καὶ μέγα ποτ’ ἀπαπνεύσειαν εἰς ἅπαξ, οἷον ἀποπειρώμενοι τῆς τοιαύτης ἀναπνοῆς, ἀφίστανται παραχρῆμα διὰ τὴν ὀδύνην, καὶ χρόνῳ γε παμπόλλῳ μικρὸν πάνυ ἀναπνέουσιν, ἄχρι περ ἂν ὑπὸ τῆς χρείας ἐπειγούσης ἀναγκασθέντες ἐφ’ ἑτέραν αὖθις πεῖραν τράπωνται μεγάλης ἀναπνοῆς.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For even if at some time they should breathe largely once (ἀπαπνεύσειαν), as though making trial of such a breath, they desist at once on account of the pain, and for a very long time they breathe quite small, until, compelled by the urgent need, they turn once again to another attempt at a large breath.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For even if at some point they should take a large breath (reading ἀπαπνεύσειαν as 'breathe') all at once, as if making trial of such breathing, they immediately desist because of the pain, and for a very long time they breathe very small, until, compelled by the pressing need, they turn once more to another attempt at a large breath.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ἄτακτ-ος, ον, not in battle-order, of troops, Hdt. 6.93 , Th. 8.105 ( Comp. ). not at one's post, Lycurg. 39 . undisciplined, disorderly, θόρυβος Th. 8.10 ; ποιεῖν τὴν πολιτείαν ἀτακτοτέραν Arist. Pol. 1319b15 ; irregular, πυρετός Hp. Coac. 26 ; οὐδὲν ἄ. τῶν φύσει Arist. Ph. 252a11 ; φθορὰ ἄ. casual, Id. HA 556a12 ; of sensual excess, irregular, inordinate, ἡδοναί, Ἀφροδίτη, Pl. Lg. 660b , 840e ; in Music, without rhythm, μελῳδίαι Aristid.Quint. 1.13 ; Medic., irregular, σφυγμός Gal. 8.458 . uncivilized, lawless, βίος Critias 25.1 D. Math., ἄτακτα προβλήματα indeterminate, not admitting of a definite solution, Procl. in Euc. p.220 F. Adv. -τως in an irregular, disorderly manner, of troops, ἀ. καὶ οὐδενὶ κόσμῳ προσπίπτοντες Th. 3.108 ; ἀ. διώκειν Id. 2.91 ; ἀτακτότερον προσπεσόντες Id. 6.97 , cf. X. Cyr. 1.4.22 , Hell.Oxy. 6.4 ; ἀ. φέρεσθαι Isoc. 1.32 ; οὐθὲν ἀ. θεῷ πράττεται Epicur. Ep. 3p.65U. irregularly, of fevers, Hp. Epid. 1.7 ; ζῆν Isoc. 2.31 . Comp. ἀτακτοτέρως somewhat negligently, Demetr. Eloc. 53 .
term_table.greek_sentence: τὸ συνεχὲς οὖν τῆς ἀνωμαλίας καὶ ἀτάκτου μεταβολῆς αὐτοῖς ἐν τάχει καὶ βραδυτῆτι καὶ ταῖς τῆς πυκνότητος ἐξαλλαγαῖς μάλιστα συνίσταται, μηδέποτε μὲν ἁπλῶς ἀραιᾶς γιγνομένης τῆς ἀναπνοῆς διὰ τὴν τῆς χρείας ἔπειξιν, ἧττον μέντοι καὶ μᾶλλον πυκνῆς, κᾀν τούτῳ τὴν ἀνωμαλίαν κτωμένης.
term_table.english_sentence_A: The continuity, then, of the irregularity and of the disordered change in them consists chiefly in speed and slowness and in the alterations of frequency, the respiration never becoming simply rare, on account of the urgency of the need, yet being less and more frequent, and in this acquiring its irregularity.
term_table.english_sentence_B: The continuity of their unevenness and disordered change, then, consists chiefly in speed and slowness and in the variations of frequency. Because of the urgency of the need, the breathing never becomes simply infrequent; it becomes more and less frequent, and in this it acquires its unevenness.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ὀξύ-ρροπος, ον, turning quickly, prop. of a delicate balance : metaph., ὀ. πρὸς τὰς ὀργάς sudden and quick to anger, Pl. Tht. 144a ; εἰς ὀργήν Jul. term_table.greek_sentence: ὥστ’ ἔστι πυκνὸν μὲν ἀεὶ τοῖς οὕτω διακειμένοις τὸ πνεῦμα, μέγα δὲ σπανίως, βραδὺ δ’ οὐδὲν μᾶλλον ἢ ταχὺ, διὰ τὴν εἰς ἑκάτερον αὐτῶν ὀξύῤῥοπον μετάπτωσιν.
term_table.english_sentence_A: So that in those who are so disposed the breath is always frequent, large rarely, and slow no more than quick, on account of the abrupt shift toward either of them.
term_table.english_sentence_B: So in those who are so disposed the breath is always frequent, rarely large, and no more slow than fast, because of its quick-tipping transition into either of these.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: παραφροσύνη, ἡ, wandering of mind, derangement, Pl. Sph. 228d , Aps. p.333 H. delirium, Hp. Aph. 2.2 , 6.53 (pl.), Prog. 10 .
term_table.greek_sentence: ὀρθῶς οὖν ἔμπροσθεν ἐῤῥέθη πᾶσι τοῖς ὀργάνοις ὀδυνωμένοις, ὅσα κινεῖται κατὰ τὰς ἀναπνοὰς, μικρὸν καὶ πυκνὸν ἕπεσθαι τὸ πνεῦμα· κατὰ δὲ τὸν αὐτὸν λόγον ἐν ταῖς παραφροσύναις μέγα τε γίγνεσθαι καὶ ἀραιὸν, εἰ καὶ ὅτι μάλιστα [809] καὶ ταύταις ἀνωμαλία τις ἕπεται.
term_table.english_sentence_A: Rightly, then, was it said earlier that in all the organs that are moved in respiration, when they are in pain, the breathing that follows is small and frequent; and by the same reasoning that in deliriums it becomes large and rare, even if, most especially, [809] some unevenness attends these too.
term_table.english_sentence_B: It was therefore rightly said earlier that, when any of the organs moved in respiration is in pain, small and frequent breathing follows; and, by the same reasoning, that in deliria the breathing becomes large and infrequent, even though some irregularity very much [809] attends these too.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ἀραιό-της, ητος, ἡ, looseness of substance, porousness, rarity, opp. πυκνότης, Hp. Aph. 5.63 , al., Arist. Pr. 869b30 : pl., Id. Ph. 260b10 , Epicur. Ep. 2p.49U. , Placit. 3.12.1 ; τῶν πόρων Arist. Aud. 802a24 ; opp. πύκνωσις, Plu. Fr.inc. 149 .
term_table.greek_sentence: πλεονεκτεῖ γὰρ ἐν αὐταῖς ἥ τε ἀραιότης καὶ τὸ μέγεθος· μᾶλλον μὲν γὰρ καὶ ἧττον ἀραιὸν καὶ μᾶλλον καὶ ἧττον μέγα τοῖς παραφρονοῦσι γίγνεται τὸ πνεῦμα, μικρὸν δὲ καὶ πυκνὸν οὐδέποτε.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For in them rarity and largeness predominate; for the breathing of those who are delirious becomes more and less rare, and more and less large, but never small and frequent.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For in them infrequency and largeness predominate: in those who are delirious the breathing becomes more or less infrequent and more or less large, but never small and frequent.

term_table.greek_sentence: τοσαῦτα ἀρκεῖν μοι δοκεῖ περὶ τῶν ἀνωμαλιῶν εἰδέναι τῶν τε κατὰ μίαν ἐνέργειαν καὶ τῶν ἐν πλείοσι συνισταμένων.
term_table.english_sentence_A: So much seems to me sufficient to know about the unevennesses, both those occurring in a single activity and those constituted in several.
term_table.english_sentence_B: This much seems to me sufficient to know about the irregularities, both those in a single activity and those that arise in several.

term_table.greek_sentence: καὶ μέντοι σαφῶς μὲν αὗται σύνθετοι, παμπόλλων ἐνεργειῶν εἰς γένεσίν τε καὶ διάγνωσιν δεόμεναι· αἱ δὲ κατὰ μίαν, ὡς καὶ πρόσθεν εἴρηται, τάχ’ ἄν τῳ δόξειαν ὑπάρχειν ἁπλαῖ.
term_table.english_sentence_A: And indeed these latter are clearly composite, requiring very many activities both for their generation and for their diagnosis; whereas those in a single activity, as was also said before, might perhaps seem to someone to be simple.
term_table.english_sentence_B: And indeed these latter are clearly compound, since they require a great many activities both for their generation and for their diagnosis; whereas those in a single activity, as was also said before, might perhaps seem to someone to be simple.

term_table.greek_sentence: καὶ μέντοι σαφῶς μὲν αὗται σύνθετοι, παμπόλλων ἐνεργειῶν εἰς γένεσίν τε καὶ διάγνωσιν δεόμεναι· αἱ δὲ κατὰ μίαν, ὡς καὶ πρόσθεν εἴρηται, τάχ’ ἄν τῳ δόξειαν ὑπάρχειν ἁπλαῖ.
term_table.english_sentence_A: And indeed these latter are clearly composite, requiring very many activities both for their generation and for their diagnosis; whereas those in a single activity, as was also said before, might perhaps seem to someone to be simple.
term_table.english_sentence_B: And indeed these latter are clearly compound, since they require a great many activities both for their generation and for their diagnosis; whereas those in a single activity, as was also said before, might perhaps seem to someone to be simple.

term_table.english_sentence_A: And we have gone through, in the same place, not only the systematic unevennesses but also the disorders.
term_table.english_sentence_B: In the same discussion we went through not only the systematic irregularities but also the instances of disorder.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: εἰσπνοή, ἡ, inspiration, inhalation, opp. ἐκπνοή, Arist. Resp. 471a8 , cf. Str. 3.5.7 ; μιᾷ ἐσπνοῇ θνῄσκουσι Aret. SA 1.7 .
term_table.greek_sentence: ἡ μὲν δὴ μεγάλη τε καὶ ἅμα ταχεῖα εἰσπνοὴ τῆς μὲν χρείας ἐπειγούσης γίνεται, τῶν δ’ ὀργάνων εὐπειθῶν ὑπαρχόντων, τῆς [810] δυνάμεως δὲ ἤτοι τὴν ἰδίαν εὐρωστίαν εὐρωστούσης, ἢ μικρὸν μεταβεβλημένης.
term_table.english_sentence_A: Now the inspiration that is large and at the same time rapid occurs when the need is pressing, the organs are compliant, and the [810] faculty either enjoys its own proper vigour or has been altered only a little.
term_table.english_sentence_B: A large and at the same time fast inspiration occurs when the need is pressing, the instruments are compliant, and the [810] faculty either is strong with its own proper strength or has been only slightly altered.

term_table.greek_sentence: ἡ δὲ λοιπὴ καὶ τετάρτη συζυγία μικρότης ἦν ἅμα τῷ τάχει καὶ γίγνεται διὰ παντὸς μὲν ἐπ’ οὐδεμιᾷ διαθέσει ἁπλῇ, καθάπερ οὐδὲ ἡ μεγάλη τε ἅμα καὶ βραδεῖα, ἣν ἔσθ’ ὅτε τοῖς παραπαίουσι συμπίπτειν ἔφαμεν· ἕπεται μέντοι κᾂν εἰ μὴ διηνεκῶς, ἀλλ’ ὡς τὸ πολύ γε, συνελθόντων εἰς ταὐτὸν ἀλγήματός τε καὶ χρείας αὐξήσεως.
term_table.english_sentence_A: The remaining and fourth conjugation was smallness together with rapidity, and it occurs constantly in no simple condition, just as neither does the large and at the same time slow inspiration, which we said sometimes befalls those who are delirious; it does follow, however, if not continuously, at least for the most part, when pain and an increase of the need come together in the same patient.
term_table.english_sentence_B: It does not invariably arise upon any simple condition, just as the inspiration that is large and at the same time slow does not either, which we said sometimes befalls those who are deranged. It does, however, follow, if not continually, at least for the most part, when pain and an increase of the need come together in the same person.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: οὐδείς, fem. οὐδεμία (never nom. acc. -μίη, -μίην, since οὐδεμιῇ is prob. in Call. Aet.Oxy. 2080.56 , rarely οὐδ' ἴα Sapph. 69 , Mosch. 4.40 ), neut. οὐδέν (declined and accentuated like εἷς, μία, ἕν ), not one, i.e. no one, none, used by Hom. , Hes. , and Pi. (who prefer οὔτις) only in neut. nom. and acc. οὐδέν, exc. in the phrase τὸ ὃν μένος οὐδενὶ εἴκων Il. 22.459 , al.; οὐδείς is found in B. Fr. 28 ; but all genders and cases are common in all other writers, Hdt. 1.32 , 33 , etc.: rare in pl., no set of persons or things, And. 1.23 (dub. cj.), X. Lac. 3.1 ; πρὸς οὐδένας τῶν Ἑλλήνων D. 18.23 (v.l.), cf. 19.31 , 66 , 312 , 24.214 , 27.7 ; οὐδένων εἰσὶ βελτίους, i.e. οὔ τινων ἄλλων, Id. 2.17 (cf. οὐδενὸς βελτίους Pl. Prt. 324d ): dat. pl. οὐδέσιν Paus. 3.24.3 ; for another sense of the pl., v. infr. 11.3 .—In Ion. the pl. is usu. οὐδαμοί. οὐ. ὅστις οὐ every one, Hdt. 3.72 , etc.; οὐδὲν ὅ τι οὐ every, Id. 5.97 ; this came to be regarded as one word, so that οὐδείς passed into the same case as ὅστις, οὐδένα ὅντινα οὐ κατέκλασε Pl. Phd. 117d ; οὐδενὸς ὅτου οὐ πάντων ἂν . . πατὴρ εἴην Id. Prt. 317c , cf. 323b ; οὐδενὶ ὅτῳ οὐκ ἀποκρινόμενος Id. Men. 70c ; so οὐ. ὃς οὐχὶ . . ὀνειδιεῖ S. OT 373 ; οὐδὲν γὰρ . . οὔτ' αἰσχρὸν οὔτ' ἄτιμόν ἐσθ', ὁποῖον οὐ . . οὐκ ὄπωπ' ἐγώ Id. Ant. 4 . later οὐδὲν ὅ τι without οὐ, = nothing, οὐδὲν ὅ τι παρήσω Agath. Praef. p.137 D. , al. ὅστις οὐδείς not one, ἐτεθνήκεσαν δὲ αὐτῶν μὲν ἀμφὶ τοὺς τετρακοσίους, Ρωμαίων δὲ ὅστις οὐδείς Id. 5.20 . naught, good for naught, ὦ νῦν μὲν οὐ. αὔριον δ' ὑπέρμεγας Ar. Eq. 158 , cf. E. Fr. 187.5 ; τὸ μὲν [γένος ἀνδρῶν] οὐδέν Pi. N. 6.3 : freq. in neut., οὐδὲν εἰδώς knowing naught, Thgn. 141 , E. Fr. 391 ; οὐκ ἄρ' ᾔστην οὐδὲν ἄλλο πλὴν δάκνειν knew nothing save how to . . , Ar. Av. 19 ; οὐδὲν λέγειν to say naught, v. λέγω (B) III. 6 ; τὸ οὐδ' οὐδέν the absolute nothing, Pl. Tht. 180a . in neut., of persons, οὐδέν εἰμι S. Ph. 951 , etc.; οὐδὲν εἶ Ar. Ec. 144 ; πρὸς τὸν οὐδέν E. Ph. 598 ; τὸ μηδὲν εἰς οὐδὲν ῥέπει Id. Fr. 532.2 ; ᾧ ἀνεμέσητον . . οὐδενὶ εἶναι Pl. Tht. 175e . in pl., οὐδένες ἐόντες ἐν οὐδαμοῖσι ἐοῦσι Ἕλλησι being nobodies, Hdt. 9.58 ; ὄντες οὐδένες E. Andr. 700 , cf. IA 371 ; ὁ μηδὲν ὢν κἀξ οὐδένων κεκλήσομαι dub. cj. in Id. Ion 594 ; οὐ γὰρ ἠξίου τοὺς μηδένας S. Aj. 1114 . with Preps., παρ' οὐδὲν εἶναι Id. OT 983 , etc.; παρ' οὐδὲν ἄγειν, θέσθαι, Id. Ant. 35 , E. IT 732 ; δι' οὐδενὸς ποιεῖσθαι S. OC 584 ; ἐν οὐδενὸς εἶναι μέρει D. 2.18 . τὸ οὐδέν naught, zero, in Arith., Nicom. Ar. 2.6 ; used by Democritus as a name for Place, Arist. Fr. 208 . neut. οὐδέν as Adv., not at all, naught, ἄριστον Ἀχαιῶν οὐ. ἔτισεν Il. 1.412 , cf. 24.370 , Hdt. 5.34 , Th. 8.22 , etc.; so οὐδέν τι X. Mem. 1.2.42 , etc.; οὐ. τι πάντως Hdt. 5.65 : in answers, nothing, never mind, no matter, E. Med. 64 , IT 781 , Ar. Nu. 694 ; οὐδέν γε not at all, Id. Av. 1360 , etc.; οὐδὲν μᾶλλον, οὐδὲν ἧσσον, οὐδὲν ὕστερος, v. μάλα 11.5 , ἥσσων 111 , ὕστερος A. I. οὐδὲν ἄλλο ἤ, v. ἄλλος III. 2 . REMARKS: the more emphatic and literal sense, not even one, i.e. none whatever, belongs to the full form, οὐδὲ εἷς, οὐδὲ μία, οὐδὲ ἕν, which is never elided, even in Com. (v. Ar. Ra. 927 , Lys. 1045 (lyr.), Pl. 138 , 1115 ), but freq. has a Particle inserted between, cf. οὐδέ B. — Zen. (in EM 639.17 ) and others wrongly assume οὐδείς as a compd. not of οὐδέ and εἷς, but of οὐ and δείς (q. v.). (Later οὐθείς, q. v.)

term_table.greek_sentence: ἡ δὲ λοιπὴ καὶ τετάρτη συζυγία μικρότης ἦν ἅμα τῷ τάχει καὶ γίγνεται διὰ παντὸς μὲν ἐπ’ οὐδεμιᾷ διαθέσει ἁπλῇ, καθάπερ οὐδὲ ἡ μεγάλη τε ἅμα καὶ βραδεῖα, ἣν ἔσθ’ ὅτε τοῖς παραπαίουσι συμπίπτειν ἔφαμεν· ἕπεται μέντοι κᾂν εἰ μὴ διηνεκῶς, ἀλλ’ ὡς τὸ πολύ γε, συνελθόντων εἰς ταὐτὸν ἀλγήματός τε καὶ χρείας αὐξήσεως.
term_table.english_sentence_A: The remaining and fourth conjugation was smallness together with rapidity, and it occurs constantly in no simple condition, just as neither does the large and at the same time slow inspiration, which we said sometimes befalls those who are delirious; it does follow, however, if not continuously, at least for the most part, when pain and an increase of the need come together in the same patient.
term_table.english_sentence_B: It does not invariably arise upon any simple condition, just as the inspiration that is large and at the same time slow does not either, which we said sometimes befalls those who are deranged. It does, however, follow, if not continually, at least for the most part, when pain and an increase of the need come together in the same person.

term_table.greek_sentence: μικρὸν μὲν γὰρ ἐν τοῖς ἀλγήμασιν ἐξ ἀνάγκης ἀναπνέουσιν, ἀπληρώτου δὲ τῆς χρείας μενούσης, διά τε τὴν αὐτὴν ταύτην μικρότητα καὶ ὅτι πλεονεκτεῖν ὑπέκειτο καθ’ ἑαυτὴν, οὐκ ἀρκεῖ πυκνωθῆναι μόνον τὰς ἐνεργείας, ἀλλ’ ἀναγκάζονται πολλάκις ἐσπασμένως εἰσπνεῖν.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For in pains they necessarily breathe small; and since the need remains unfulfilled, both because of this very smallness and because it was assumed to be in excess on its own account, it does not suffice for the activities merely to become frequent, but they are often compelled to breathe in in a spasmodic manner.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For in pains they of necessity breathe small. Since the need remains unfulfilled, both because of this very smallness and because it was assumed to be in excess on its own account, it is not enough that the activities merely be made frequent; they are often compelled to breathe in spasmodically.

term_table.greek_sentence: φαίνεται γὰρ ἐναργῶς ἐπὶ τούτου δριμέα πάντα καὶ θερμὰ τὰ καπνώδη τῆς ὕλης περιττώματα, ἐνδεικνύμενα δεδέχθαι μὲν εἰς ἑαυτὰ τὴν τοῦ πυρὸς δύναμιν, οὐ μὴν πάντα γε ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ κεκρατῆσθαι· φλὸξ γὰρ ἂν οὕτως ἐγεγόνει καὶ οὐκέτι καπνός.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For in the case of the latter all the smoky residues of the material plainly appear acrid and hot, showing that they have indeed received into themselves the power of the fire, yet have not been entirely mastered by it; for in that case flame would have come to be, and no longer smoke.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For in the case of fire it is plainly evident that all the smoky residues of the material are acrid and hot, which indicates that they have received into themselves the power of the fire, yet have not been wholly mastered by it; for in that case flame would have come into being, and no longer smoke.

term_table.greek_sentence: ὥστε εἴ τις θερμασίας καπνώδους ἐν τοῖς σώμασι τῶν ζώων πλεονεκτούσης, τὴν ἐκπνοὴν λέγοι μεγάλην τε ἅμα γίνεσθαι καὶ ταχεῖαν, οὐκ ἂν ἁμάρτοι· δῆλον δ’ ὅτι καὶ τὴν δύναμιν ἐῤῥῶσθαι χρὴ τηνικαῦτα, καὶ τῶν ὀργάνων μηδὲν πεπονθέναι· κατὰ ταὐτὰ δὲ καὶ τὴν μεγάλην τε ἅμα καὶ βραδεῖαν ἐνίοις τῶν παραφρονούντων, ὥσπερ εἶχε κᾀπὶ τῆς εἰσπνοῆς· οὕτω δὲ καὶ τὴν μικρὰν ἅμα καὶ βραδεῖαν, οἷς μηδὲν [812] συνήθροιστο καπνῶδες περίττωμα, καὶ τὴν μικρὰν καὶ ταχεῖαν, οἷς ἤθροιστο, καὶ ὀδυνᾶται τῶν μορίων ὅσα δηλονότι κινεῖται κατὰ τὰς ἀναπνοάς.
term_table.english_sentence_A: So that if someone were to say that, when smoky heat predominates in the bodies of animals, the expiration becomes both great and at the same time rapid, he would not err; and it is clear that at that time the faculty must also be strong, and none of the organs must be affected. In the same way, too, the expiration that is both great and at the same time slow occurs in some of those who are delirious, just as was the case with inspiration as well; and so too the small and at the same time slow one, in those in whom no [812] smoky residue has accumulated, and the small and rapid one, in those in whom it has accumulated and in whom there is pain in those parts, namely, which are moved in respiration.
term_table.english_sentence_B: So that if someone were to say that, when smoky heat predominates in the bodies of animals, the expiration becomes at once large and fast, he would not be wrong; but it is clear that at that time the faculty must also be strong, and none of the organs must be affected. In the same way he would not be wrong in saying that the expiration which is at once large and slow occurs in some of those who are delirious, just as was the case with inspiration; and likewise the small and at the same time slow expiration in those in whom no smoky residue had [812] accumulated, and the small and fast in those in whom it had accumulated and in whom those of the parts that are, evidently, moved in respiration are in pain.

term_table.english_sentence_B: So that if someone were to say that, when smoky heat predominates in the bodies of animals, the expiration becomes at once large and fast, he would not be wrong; but it is clear that at that time the faculty must also be strong, and none of the organs must be affected. In the same way he would not be wrong in saying that the expiration which is at once large and slow occurs in some of those who are delirious, just as was the case with inspiration; and likewise the small and at the same time slow expiration in those in whom no smoky residue had [812] accumulated, and the small and fast in those in whom it had accumulated and in whom those of the parts that are, evidently, moved in respiration are in pain.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: συζυγ-ία, ἡ,= σύζευξις, union, E. HF 675 (lyr.); union of branches with the trunk, ς. τῶν φλεβῶν Arist. HA 586b21 . yoke of animals, pair, ς. πώλων E. Hipp. 1131 (lyr.); of persons, Plu. Demetr. 1 : generally, pair, Pl. Phd. 71c , Prm. 143d , Arist. IA 704b20 ; ς. πτερύγων, μήλων, δονάκων, AP 5.267.6 , 289 (both Paul. Sil.), 6.27 ( Theaet. ); ἄρσενα ς., of two sons, IG 12(8).442.6 (Thasos); κατὰ συζυγίας in pairs, esp. of animals, κατὰ συζυγίας φωλοῦσιν . . οἱ ἄρρενες θήλεσιν Arist. HA 599b6 , cf. 631b1 ; in plants, Thphr. HP 3.11.3 , al.: hence, coupling, copulation, AP 5.220 (Paul. Sil.), 10.68 ( Agath. ). in war, squadron of four war-chariots,= two ζυγαρχίαι, Ascl. Tact. 8 , Ael. Tact. 22.2 . conjunction of words or things in pairs, syzygy, Arist. Top. 113a12 , GC 332b3 (pl.), Mete. 378b11 (pl.), Stoic. 2.132 , Gal. 6.95 , al.: more generally, combination of words, οὐκ ἐν τῷ κάλλει τῶν ὀνομάτων ἡ πειθώ, ἀλλ' ἐν τῇ ς. D.H. Comp. 3 , cf. 6 ; of letters, ib. 22 ; coupling of terms in a syllogism, Chrysipp.Stoic. 2.50 . Gramm., conjugation, D.T. 638.6 (pl.), A.D. Adv. 161.28 , POxy. 469.13 (iii A.D.); or declension, A.D. Adv. 198.6 , Synt. 271.16 , Ath. 9.392b ; any group of related words, e.g. sapiens, sapienter, sapientia, Cic. Top. 3.12 , cf. 9.38 . in Prosody, syzygy, dipodia, Heph. 7.8 , Aristid. Quint. 1.14 , Syrian. in Hermog. 1p.31R. syncope, Anon.Rhythm. 3.19 . Astron., syzygy, of two stars one of which rises and sets as the other sets and rises, Autol. 1.4 ; of zodiacal signs rising and setting between the same points of the horizon, Gem. 2.27 ; of the moon's conjunctions and oppositions with the sun, Ptol. Alm. 5.1 , Cat.Cod.Astr. 1.131 ; so of planets, Ptol. Alm. 5.10 . Math., αἱ κατὰ συζυγίαν ἀντικείμεναι [τομαί] conjugate opposite sections, i.e. conjugate hyperbolas, each with two branches, Apollon.Perg. Con. 2.17 , al.
term_table.greek_sentence: Αὗται μὲν οὖν αἱ τέτταρες συζυγίαι τῶν δυσπνοιῶν καθ’ ἑκάτερον ἰδίᾳ τῆς ὅλης ἀναπνοῆς μόριον συνίστανται· ἕτεραι δὲ κατὰ τὸν οἷον ῥυθμὸν αὐτῆς, οὐ καθ’ ἑκάτερον, ὅταν δὲ παραβάλλωμεν εἰσπνοὴν ἐκπνοῇ, καθάπερ ἐν τοῖς σφυγμοῖς διαστολὴν συστολῇ, ῥυθμὸν τὸ τοιοῦτον ὀνομάζομεν.
term_table.english_sentence_A: These four conjugations of dyspnoeas, then, are constituted in each part of the whole respiration taken separately; but others are constituted according to what may be called its rhythm, not in each part [separately]; and when we compare inspiration with expiration, just as in the pulses diastole with systole, we name such a thing rhythm.
term_table.english_sentence_B: These, then, are the four combinations of the dyspnoeas that are constituted in each part of the whole respiration separately; but there are others according to what is, as it were, its rhythm, not in each part separately: when we compare inspiration with expiration, just as in the pulses diastole with systole, we call such a thing rhythm.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ῥυθμός, Ion. ῥυσμός (v. infr. 111 , IV), ὁ: (ῥέω):— any regular recurring motion ( πᾶς ῥ. ὡρισμένῃ μετρεῖται κινήσει Arist. Pr. 882b2 ): measured motion, time, whether in sound or motion, Democr. 15c ; = ἡ τῆς κινήσεως τάξις , Pl. Lg. 665a , cf. 672e ; ὁ ῥ. ἐκ τοῦ ταχέος καὶ βραδέος, ἐκ διενηνεγμένων πρότερον, ὕστερον δὲ ὁμολογησάντων γέγονε Id. Smp. 187b , cf. Suid. s.v.; rhythm, opp. μέτρον and ἁρμονία, Ar. Nu. 638 sq., Pl. R. 397b , 398d , 601a , Arist. Rh. 1403b31 ; λόγοι μετὰ μουσικῆς καὶ ῥυθμῶν πεποιημένοι Isoc. 15.46 ; of Prose rhythm, Arist. Rh. 1408b29 , D.H. Comp. 17 : defined by Aristox. Rhyth. 1 , Aristid.Quint. 1.13 . special phrases: ἐν ῥυθμῷ in time, of dancing, marching, etc., βαίνειν ἐν ῥ. Pl. Lg. 670b , cf. X. An. 5.4.14 ; ὀρχεῖσθαι Id. Cyr. 1.3.10 ; ἐν τῷ ῥ. ἀναπνεῖν respire regularly, Arist. Pr. 882b1 ; so σωζόμενος ῥ. A. Ch. 797 (lyr.); μετὰ ῥυθμοῦ βαίνοντες Th. 5.70 ; ῥυθμὸν χορείας ὑπάγειν keep time, Ar. Th. 956 (lyr.); θάττονα ῥυθμὸν ἐπάγειν play in quicker time, X. Smp. 2.22 ; πυρριχίῳ δρόμῳ καὶ ῥυθμῷ Hdn. 4.2.9 , cf. Plb. 4.20.6 : pl., paces, Alcid. Soph. 17 . measure, proportion or symmetry of parts, at rest as well as in motion, κατὰ τὸν αὐτὸν ῥ. Pl. Lg. 728e . generally, proportion, arrangement, order, ῥυθμῷ τινι E. Cyc. 398 (codd., but θ' ἑνὶ is prob.); οὐκ ἀπὸ ῥυσμοῦ εἰκάζω not without reason, Call. Epigr. 44.5 . state or condition of anything, temper, disposition, Thgn. 964 (coupled with ὀργή and τρόπος) ; οἷος ῥυσμὸς ἀνθρώπους ἔχει Archil. 66.7 ; ὅσοι χθονίους ἔχουσι ῥυσμοὺς καὶ χαλεπούς Anacr. 74 ; μένει . . χρῆμ' οὐδὲν ἐν ταὐτῷ ῥ. Eup. 356 . form, shape of a thing, Democr. 5i ; identified by Arist. with σχῆμα, Metaph. 985b16 , 1042b14 ; μετέβαλον τὸν ῥ. τῶν γραμμάτων changed the form or shape of the letters, Hdt. 5.58 ; of Chian boots, Hp. Art. 62 ; of the shape of a cup, Alex. 59 ; of a breastplate, X. Mem. 3.10.10 ; [τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου] LXX 4 Ki. 16.10 ; Αὐτονόας ῥ. ωὑτός Theoc. 26.23 ; so of the natural features of a country, D.P. 271 , 620 ; structure of a substance, κεγχροειδὲς τῷ ῥ., τῷ ῥ. σπογγῶδες, Dsc. 5.77 , 118 . manner, fashion of a thing, Ἕλλην ῥ. πέπλων E. Heracl. 130 ; τίνι ῥ. φόνου; by what kind of slaughter? Id. El. 772 , cf. Supp. 94 ; ἐν τριγώνοις ῥυθμοῖς triangular-wise, A. Fr. 78 . [υ by nature, A. Ch. 797 (lyr.), E. Supp. 94 , etc.; υ by position in Thgn. 964 , etc.]

term_table.greek_sentence: εἴρηται μὲν οὖν ἡμῖν περὶ αὐτῶν ὅσα χρὴ κᾀν ταῖς περὶ τῶν σφυγμῶν πραγματείαις· εἰρήσεται δὲ καὶ νῦν ὅσον οἷόν τε διὰ βραχυτάτων, οἷς χρὴ προσέχοντα τὸν νοῦν οἷον σκοποῖς τισιν ἐξευρίσκειν τὰς αἰτίας ῥᾳδίως τῆς ἐν ταῖς ἀναπνοαῖς ἀῤῥυθμίας.
term_table.english_sentence_A: We have, then, said all that is needed about them also in the treatises on the pulses; but it will be stated now too, as far as possible in the briefest terms, what things one must attend to, as to certain targets, in order to discover easily the causes of arrhythmia in respirations.
term_table.english_sentence_B: We have, then, said what is needed about them in the treatises on the pulses as well; but they will be stated now also, as briefly as possible: the points to which one must direct one's attention, as to certain marks, in order readily to discover the causes of the lack of rhythm in respirations.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: εἰσπνοή, ἡ, inspiration, inhalation, opp. ἐκπνοή, Arist. Resp. 471a8 , cf. Str. 3.5.7 ; μιᾷ ἐσπνοῇ θνῄσκουσι Aret. SA 1.7 .
term_table.greek_sentence: τὰ γὰρ ἄρτι καθ’ ἑκάτερον τῆς ὅλης ἀναπνοῆς ﻿ [813] μό ριον, τήν τε εἰσπνοὴν λέγω καὶ τὴν ἐκπνοὴν, ἅπερ ἐν τῷ πρόσθεν λόγῳ φθάνομεν εἰρηκότες, αὐτὰ ταῦτα καὶ νῦν ἀξιῶ σκοπεῖσθαι κατὰ τὰς ἀῤῥυθμίας αὐτῶν.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For the points which we have just made in the preceding discussion concerning each part of the whole respiration [813] severally—I mean inspiration and expiration—these very points I ask that one consider now as well with regard to their arrhythmias.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For the very things I just set out concerning each [813] part of the whole respiration (I mean inspiration and expiration), which we have already stated in the preceding discussion, these same things I think it right to consider now also with respect to their arrhythmias.

term_table.greek_sentence: οἷον, οὐδὲν γὰρ χεῖρον ἐφ’ ἑνός τινος ὡς ἐπὶ παραδείγματος ἐπιδεῖξαι τὸ λεγόμενον, βραδυτέρα μὲν ἔστω καὶ μικροτέρα τοῦ κατὰ φύσιν εἰσπνοὴ, θάττων δὲ καὶ μείζων ἡ ἐκπνοή· μεμειῶσθαι φήσομεν τοῖς οὕτω διακειμένοις τὸ κατὰ φύσιν θερμὸν, ηὐξῆσθαι δὲ τὸ καπνῶδες.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For example—for it is no worse to demonstrate what is being said in some single case by way of illustration—let the inspiration be slower and smaller than the natural one, but the expiration faster and larger: we shall say that in those so disposed the natural heat has been diminished, while the smoky heat has been increased.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For example (there is nothing wrong with demonstrating what is being said on some one case, as an example), let inspiration be slower and smaller than the natural, and expiration quicker and larger: we shall say that in those so disposed the natural heat has been diminished and the smoky has been increased.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: μικρός and σμικρός, ά, όν, Dor. , Ion. μικκός (q.v.): σμικρός is corroborated by metre in Il. 17.757 , Hes. Op. 361 , and might be restored in Il. 5.801 , Od. 3.296 (μικρός codd.); it is prob. the only form in Hdt. ( μικρός Hdt. 2.74 codd.): freq. in Lyr. and prob. always in Trag. (exc. where metre requires μικρός, as S. Aj. 161 (anap., Comp. )); most freq. in Pl. ; but in Th. , also Ar. and other Com., μικρός prevails, σμικρός being found Th. 4.13 , 7.75 , 8.81 , Ar. Ach. 523 , V. 5 ; Att. Inscrr. have σμικρός IG 12.313.111 , al., μικρός ib. 369.10 , al.:—small, little, in Size, μ. ἔην δέμας Il. 5.801 ; μ. λίθος Od. 3.296 ; κίρκον, ὅ τε σμικρῇσι φόνον φέρει ὀρνίθεσσιν Il. 17.757 ; σμ. ἄστεα Hdt. 1.5 ; μεγάθεϊ σμικροί Id. 2.74 : with Dims., μ. πολίχνιον, γῄδιον, παιδάρια, Isoc. 5.145 , X. Pol. 1311b3 ; οἱ ἐν μικρῷ μεγάλοι short but stoutly built, Philostr. Gym. 36 ; ὁ μ. δάκτυλος SIG 1172.4 (Lebena). in Quantity, σμικρὸν ἐπὶ σμικρῷ καταθεῖναι Hes. Op. 361 ; μέλιτος μικρόν Ar. term_table.greek_sentence: οἷον, οὐδὲν γὰρ χεῖρον ἐφ’ ἑνός τινος ὡς ἐπὶ παραδείγματος ἐπιδεῖξαι τὸ λεγόμενον, βραδυτέρα μὲν ἔστω καὶ μικροτέρα τοῦ κατὰ φύσιν εἰσπνοὴ, θάττων δὲ καὶ μείζων ἡ ἐκπνοή· μεμειῶσθαι φήσομεν τοῖς οὕτω διακειμένοις τὸ κατὰ φύσιν θερμὸν, ηὐξῆσθαι δὲ τὸ καπνῶδες.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For example—for it is no worse to demonstrate what is being said in some single case by way of illustration—let the inspiration be slower and smaller than the natural one, but the expiration faster and larger: we shall say that in those so disposed the natural heat has been diminished, while the smoky heat has been increased.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For example (there is nothing wrong with demonstrating what is being said on some one case, as an example), let inspiration be slower and smaller than the natural, and expiration quicker and larger: we shall say that in those so disposed the natural heat has been diminished and the smoky has been increased.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: εἰσπνοή, ἡ, inspiration, inhalation, opp. ἐκπνοή, Arist. Resp. 471a8 , cf. Str. 3.5.7 ; μιᾷ ἐσπνοῇ θνῄσκουσι Aret. SA 1.7 .
term_table.greek_sentence: εἰ γὰρ ἡ εἰσπνοὴ μικρὰ καὶ βραδεῖα τύχοι γενομένη, κατάψυξιν δηλοῖ τῆς κατὰ φύσιν θερμασίας, ὅπως ἂν ἔχῃ ἡ ἐκπνοή· εἰ δὲ ἡ ἐκπνοὴ κατὰ ταὐτὸ [814] ᾖ διακειμένη, ἐνδείξεται ταὐτόν· καὶ γὰρ εἰ μεγάλη ποτὲ καὶ ταχεῖα γένοιτο, πλεονεκτοῦσαν δηλώσει καὶ παρὰ φύσιν θερμασίαν, ὅπως ἂν ἔχῃ τὰ τῆς εἰσπνοῆς· ὅθεν οὐδὲν πλέον εἰς τὰς προγνώσεις ἡ τοιαύτη συμπλοκὴ διδάσκει τῶν ἤδη κατὰ μόνας ὑπὲρ ἑκατέρας αὐτῶν ἐγνωσμένων.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For if the inspiration should happen to become small and slow, it indicates a cooling of the natural heat, however the expiration may be disposed; and if the expiration [814] is disposed in the same way, it will indicate the same thing; for indeed if it should at some time become large and quick, it will show a heat that is in excess and contrary to nature, however the conditions of the inspiration may stand; whence such a combination teaches nothing more for prognoses than what has already been learned about each of the two separately.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For if the inspiration happens to become small and slow, it indicates a chilling of the natural heat, however the expiration may be; and if the expiration is [814] disposed in the same way, it will indicate the same thing. For again, if it should at some time become large and quick, it will indicate a heat that is excessive and contrary to nature, however matters stand with the inspiration.

term_table.english_sentence_A: We must, then, direct our attention only to those composite dyspnoeas in which the simple ones are common to several conditions and for this reason indicate nothing clear, but, when yoked together with certain others, arrive at a secure distinction.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Hence such a combination teaches nothing more towards prognoses than what is already known about each of them on its own. We must, then, turn our attention only to those compound difficulties of breathing in which the simple ones are common to several conditions, and for this reason indicate nothing clear, but, when coupled with certain others, arrive at a secure distinction.
